pool.titulo: Witcher 4 Won’t Be A PS5 Exclusive After New Deal With PlayStation
pool.resumen:
CD Projekt Red and Sony Interactive Entertainment just announced a marketing deal for The Witcher 4 , but that doesn't mean the game will be exclusive to PlayStation.
CD Projekt Red's Michał Nowakowski said on social media , "Just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform."
The marketing deal could be similar to the one between Rockstar and Sony for GTA 6, where GTA 6 was given preferential treatment on PS5 in a number of ways in the marketing campaign.
Beyond The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red is making Cyberpunk 2 , a new IP codenamed Hadar , a new game believed to be a multiplayer The Witcher title , and a remake of the original Witcher . On the mobile side, CD Projekt Red is working with Scopely on a new game that hasn't been announced yet.
The Witcher 4 now has more than 500 people working on it , and the game is expected to release in 2028. Given that timing, The Witcher 4 likely won't be on a disc because Sony won't support game discs beginning in January 2028.
That being said, CD Projekt Red is promising that The Witcher 4 will have some kind of physical goodies for fans.

pool.titulo: GTA 6’s Fake Tunnel Is A Great Way To Turn Your Muscle Car Into Scrap Metal
pool.resumen:
GTA 6 has no shortage of forces trying to put a damper on your crime spree, but the long arm of the law might be the least of your worries if you're planning a successful caper in Vice City. As players have discovered, the greatest threat to a clean getaway might just be an impressive mural, as they've smashed their vehicles right into an unforgiving wall that looks like it was ripped straight out of a Road Runner cartoon.
Located in Vice City's Decor District, this piece of street art resembles a tunnel going under the nearby overpass, and at high speed, it's pretty convincing--something I discovered to my dismay, totaling my pretty sweet muscle car in the process. Does anyone have an industrial-strength magnet so that I can start working out these dents?
It's a delicious bit of trolling from Rockstar Games: the kind of design choice that would make Looney Tunes legend Tex Avery proud with how effective it is. Numerous players have been caught out, and this is just one of many little secrets and Easter eggs hidden in the game. Fortunately, a gas station was nearby, and my muscle car limped to it for a quick repair.

pool.titulo: The Witcher 4 Wants To Be The GTA 6 Of The Witcher Franchise
pool.resumen:
There's been a massive gap between new entries in The Witcher series, and for The Witcher 4 , developer CD Projekt Red aims to make it the GTA 6 of the series, with a noticeable leap in quality. In its Q3 earnings call, the studio says it has been inspired by the technological and gameplay advancements Rockstar Games has made with GTA 6--especially when compared to 2013's GTA 5--and hopes players will feel the same way when they jump into The Witcher 4.
"First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski (via Eurogamer ). "But I do understand the connection here. Having said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences. We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4--I think so, yes. It's been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

pool.titulo: How to steal an ATM and get a winched vehicle in GTA 6
pool.resumen: Yank out ATMs and grab the cash with Yasmani's tips.
pool.contenido:
Stealing an ATM in GTA 6 requires a few different things: a winched vehicle to haul it out of the wall and drive off, plus the dye pack jammer that stops marked bills from exploding pink all over your lovely cash.
There are two ways to get a winched truck. The video above shows a location at the crop duster landing strip in Frogswater where you can steal one, but you can also mod any truck at a mod shop to add a winch.
If you don't have a truck to mod, there's a unique one you can steal from the Kolt & Associates June Warehouse robbery in Port Gellhorn, just south of Sarena's Bargain Store, which you could then register with Moses and mod at Wasteland Off-Road in the north of the town.
You'll also need the dye pack jammer, which you get in the Chapter 3 main mission, Credit Check, for Raul. Once you have both of these, you're ready to rob an ATM. If you complete all three of Yasmani's jewelry thefts (also in Chapter 3), he'll call a little later and offer tips about full ATMs, giving you three for free that you have a 24 hour window to hit. Here's how to steal them
Reverse the winched vehicle into the ATM and lower the hook with the stick until it attaches. Drive at full speed to pull the ATM out and get some distance from the sounding alarm—this will summon the cops. Smash the ATM into stuff by swerving the truck to make it spill the cash boxes Get out, kick them, and quickly grab the marked bills in each. For Yasmani's tipped-off ATMs I got about 11k-ish per time, so not terrible, but likely not the best way to make money unless you get really efficient at it and invest in a proper getaway winch truck.

pool.titulo: Even Max Verstappen has succumbed to GTA 6 fever, squeezing in 40 hours around his Las Vegas Grand Prix win
pool.resumen: What's your excuse?
pool.contenido:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has managed to get its claws into just about everyone. Honestly, I can't go anywhere without hearing something from the soundtrack or someone talking about how much fun it is to joyride around Leonida. And now it's even infested the sports I watch.
To keep non-Formula One fans up to speed, it was the Las Vegas Grand Prix over the weekend, one of the newer circuits on the calendar. Third place went to Oscar Piastri. In second place was his McLaren teammate and previous world champion for 2025, Lando Norris. And first place went to four-time F1 world champion Max Verstappen, not exactly very surprising given his history with the track. But it is a little more impressive when you take into account that Verstappen has also put 40 hours into GTA 6, much of which would have been before the race.
"I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas," he says in a stream (via IGN ), correcting the idea that he actually spent the plane ride home playing GTA 6 instead of spending time doing so around the race. "I mean I can't go out anyways [in the evening and morning], and walk around."
Verstappen did, however, explain that the aspect that GTA 6 has likely affected the most is his ability to play Minecraft, which he had planned to stream later this week: "I'm so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can't, I just can't."
GTA 6 to Minecraft is certainly a jump, but you can't really blame anyone for trying to maximise their time in Leonida right now. I'll also take any chance to spend every free moment playing the game, the only difference being that instead of subsequently competing in an F1 race and winning it, I spend the next day of work acting like a zombie—a poorly functioning one at that. I suppose people are just built differently, or at least that's what I'll tell myself while I'm on my third cup of coffee in three hours.

pool.titulo: Tangles Review
pool.resumen: Tangles Review: The Gay Nineties collide with a high-strung Jewish family in a shattering animated film about dementia.
pool.contenido:
Tangles is in theaters in New York and Los Angeles on Nov. 27. It will expand to a wider release in January.
The weight of memory is vital to the biographical animated feature Tangles, a black-and-white story about family, the queer ‘90s, and above all else, early-onset Alzheimer’s. Based on the sparse but powerful 2012 comic by Sarah Leavitt — who co-wrote the screenplay with Trev Renney and director Leah Nelson — the film employs abstractions in its margins and connective tissue, making room for straightforward drama that proves incredibly moving in its unearthing of lived experience.
Beginning with a childhood flashback, Tangles introduces us to middle-aged Midge (Julia Louis-Dreyfus), based on Leavitt’s mother, as she helps a young Sarah (Fern Grandin) fight invisible monsters in her bedroom, with the help of a flashlight which Sarah imagines as a fuchsia lightsaber. Midge is, for all intents and purposes, Sarah’s superhero, but life goes on as the film skips forward to 1999. The adult Sarah, voiced by Abbi Jacobson, draws for a queer magazine in San Francisco, but a return to her hometown for a family visit proves a major turning point. Everyone including Sarah’s soft-spoken father Rob (Bryan Cranston), her idiosyncratic aunts Debbie (Pamela Adlon) and Sukey (Sarah Silverman) and her lively sister Hannah (Beanie Feldstein) seems to dance around major changes in Midge’s lifestyle and cognitive function.
They blame it, at first, on menopause, and then on Midge losing her job and her ensuing depression, but minor tasks prove frustrating and confusing for the usually gentle 50-something, who’s drawn with appropriately haggard squiggles. It takes a while before a real diagnosis tells them what might be wrong: an early form of dementia. This forces Sarah to fly back and forth between her family and her supportive, stud girlfriend Donimo (Samira Wiley), a schism of time, place and culture that slowly wears on her as Midge’s disease advances.
The dynamic between Sarah’s queer, urban environment and her nominally accepting but high-strung Jewish family allows the film to traverse different modes of expression and conversational rhythm, as she tries to be in two places at once. This dichotomy also helps enhance periods of nerve-wracking transition during lengthy travel, expressed through tongue-in-cheek formal flourishes. Each flight, for instance, becomes the venue for dreamlike jokes about Sarah’s deep-seated anxieties delivered over the plane’s PA system, leaving her vulnerable and exposed.
Louis-Dreyfus delivers a heartrending, piercingly realistic vocal performance as a woman trying to hold on to what little of herself she can find. Sarah is a character perpetually on edge, a baseline made all the more volatile when she takes it upon herself to recognize her mother’s illness and care for her as best she can, even at the cost of her various relationships. Midge, meanwhile, slips away gradually over the film’s 102 minutes, as Louis-Dreyfus delivers a heartrending, piercingly realistic vocal performance as a woman trying to hold on to what little of herself she can find.
The period setting is rendered with appropriate details — a few too many Marvel references aside, it feels like a sketched memory of the late 1990s, from pop culture to the textures and technologies — but the story itself is timeless. Nelson brings Leavitt’s autobiographical tale to life with generosity, imbuing each supporting character with a palpable denial that feels, at first, like a mere quirk, before revealing itself to be a coping mechanism. The gradual confusion and anger involved (both for Midge and her caretakers) results in a moving portrait of helplessness in the face of a brutal disease, as well as the few moments of love people are able to steal from it while they still can. By the time the film wraps up, its echoes of Midge in earlier scenes continue to loom large thanks to Louis-Dreyfus’ fine-tuned performance as she leaves quiet gaps in her wake, alongside a sense of longing for the character she used to be.

pool.titulo: Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus
pool.resumen:
At first the kids jostle to get to the games that they know. "Welcome to the Retro Reset Bus," says Luke Stoner as the students push to get to the screen that’s caught their eye. Sonic on the Sega Mega Drive is the first they see, and the quickest student to get on board the bus looks triumphant as he nabs the stool in front of the console. Jason, Luke’s dad, asks him what he thinks about the graphics – slightly grainy and slightly pixelated – but he’s not at all bothered and soon engrossed. After a few minutes, though, his eyes keep moving to the back of the bus where "Jackson is a wally" is now emblazoned across a flickering screen in seven different colours. Jackson then gives out a chuffed yell when his code finally works after a couple of restarts. His retort to his mate appears on the 1981 BBC Micro Model B‘s screen as the other students crane to have a look. This is, incidentally, the machine that turned a national broadcaster into a computer retailer (with help from Acorn), says Jason.

Uno podría pensar que si WoW Forever es un éxito , y funciona, es principalmente por la nostalgia ; porque todos los que hemos vuelto a él lo hacemos con el fin de revivir todas esas viejas aventuras que nos fascinaron hace más de 20 años. Y parte de eso hay, claro, pero no es lo único ni por raro que parezca, lo principal. Lo digo porque lo intenté con WoW Classic y en ese momento, salí algo desencantado porque, sí, era puro World of Warcraft, pero me costó muchísimo volver a sus tiempos; a la idea de pasar horas y horas matando múrlocs deseando que cayera el objeto que necesitaba para proseguir la misión. "No tengo edad para esto", me decía a mí mismo. Curiosamente Forever es justo eso, y sin embargo me ha golpeado de una forma diferente.
Hay varios motivos que lo explican, entre ellos el hecho de que, esta vez sí, se han apuntado un montón de amigos con los que jugué a WoW por primera vez hace dos décadas. Pero aquí Blizzard también ha hecho algo genial , retocando el clásico en su justa medida; añadiendo contenidos, sumando algunas mejoras de calidad de vida, y sobre todo, dando importancia a lo verdaderamente importante: la comunidad . pool.titulo: Hoy se estrena en cines la secuela de una obra maestra de Tarantino, pero casi nadie podrá verla en la gran pantalla
pool.resumen:
Si estás en Barcelona, Madrid, Palma de Mallorca, Valencia o Zaragoza, tenemos un plan que ofrecerte para hoy: ver la secuela de una obra maestra de Quentin Tarantino dirigida por otro gran maestro del séptimo arte, David Fincher. Las nuevas desventuras de Cliff Booth llegan hoy a unos pocos cines de España antes de desembarcar en Netflix más adelante. Todo apunta a que será uno de los grandes atractivos de la cartelera ( Dunesday aparte ) en estos últimos compases del año, a unque su lanzamiento en salas sea tan, tan limitado .
Es lo que toca: la plataforma paga y, lógicamente, quiere recuperar su inversión a través de los suscriptores y no de la venta de entradas. Aun así, no deja de resultar llamativo que un largometraje dirigido por uno de los cineastas más talentosos e influyentes de los últimos treinta años tenga un paso tan limitado por las salas. Más aún cuando detrás del proyecto también está Quentin Tarantino, responsable del guion y de los personajes originales. Y sin embargo, pese a todo lo dicho, también debemos dar las gracias de tener esta opción .

pool.titulo: Achievement Unlocked: An Interview with the First XBOX Player to Reach 10 Million Gamerscore
pool.resumen:
On September 9, 2026, at 3:35pm Pacific Time, SiegfriedX unlocked a 110-point XBOX Achievement that pushed his Gamerscore to a historic 10 million. With that, he became the first XBOX player in the world to reach the milestone – just in time for XBOX’s 25th anniversary celebrations. His journey began on XBOX 360, and it […]
The post Achievement Unlocked: An Interview with the First XBOX Player to Reach 10 Million Gamerscore appeared first on XBOX Wire .
pool.contenido:
On September 9, 2026, at 3:35pm Pacific Time, SiegfriedX unlocked a 110-point XBOX Achievement that pushed his Gamerscore to a historic 10 million. With that, he became the first XBOX player in the world to reach the milestone – just in time for XBOX’s 25th anniversary celebrations.
His journey began on XBOX 360, and it took 20 years and more than 6,400 games to get there. Along the way, he has racked up some remarkable accomplishments:
What Is Gamerscore?
Gamerscore is an individual scoring system introduced with the launch of XBOX 360 in 2005. It represents the achievement points a player has earned across XBOX games.
“Since 2020, so for the past six years, I’ve unlocked at least one achievement every day,” he told XBOX Wire Brazil in an exclusive interview.
SiegfriedX is the XBOX profile of Brazilian player Marcello Malta, a 42-year-old systems analyst whose biggest hobby is hunting achievements. “I like picking up a game and unlocking every achievement, even if the last one is worth just 10 points and takes 500 hours to get. I’m still going to try,” he says.
With a milestone like that, we wanted to hear more about his passion for achievements, how it all started, and what keeps him chasing that next unlock. Here’s what he had to say.
Achievements and Gamerscore were introduced with XBOX 360. What first got you interested in achievements?
Siegfried: I was hooked on achievements right away. I didn’t even know the system existed, and I don’t think it was something people really talked about at the time. It was just a feature built into the console. You certainly didn’t buy an XBOX knowing it was there, let alone knowing it would eventually influence the entire industry and inspire similar systems elsewhere.
I remember playing and suddenly seeing that notification pop up on the screen. I thought, “What is this?” So, I looked it up, found a couple of achievement websites, started learning how the system worked, and that was it. I was hooked.
Back then, achievements really encouraged you to experience everything a game had to offer: finish the campaign, beat it on the highest difficulty, find all the collectibles, and complete specific challenges along the way. To me, they felt like the developer’s vision for how they wanted you to experience the game. Almost like they were saying, “If you’ve done all of this, you’ve seen my entire game, from beginning to end, and everything I created for you.”
What Are Achievements?
Achievements are specific goals and objectives players can complete in a game to earn Gamerscore points. Examples: finishing it on hard difficulty, collecting every collectible, or defeating a set number of opponents in multiplayer.
Each game released on XBOX includes 1,000G worth of achievements to unlock. That total can increase with additional content and expansions.
What motivates you most when it comes to chasing an achievement?
Siegfried: I first fell in love with games through Nintendo, and their games have always had that focus on collecting things and completing everything. I think that mindset stuck with me from the very beginning. achievements became an extension of that, another way of going after everything a game has to offer.
I’ve never been interested in earning points just for the sake of earning points. When I start a game, I want to unlock every achievement, even if the last one is worth just 10 points and takes 500 hours to get. I’m still going to try. I might give up or not make it in the end, but I always start with the same goal: to get everything, no matter how much time or effort it takes.
You recently reached 10 million Gamerscore. How did you plan the achievement that would take you to that milestone?
Siegfried: I wanted to hit 10 million with a game that meant something to me, something I really loved and that could make the milestone feel even more special. So I decided to do it by completing the full 1,000G in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth .
Final Fantasy is a franchise I love, so it felt like the perfect choice. The final achievement I unlocked was for beating the game on its hardest difficulty. That completed the full achievement list and brought me to exactly 10 million Gamerscore.
Was being the first player to reach 10 million Gamerscore always a goal for you?
Siegfried: I never really had a specific goal in mind. Because of the way I play, always trying to complete everything, I naturally ended up second or third in the world for Gamerscore, with someone else usually ahead of me.
Over time, though, people started dropping out, either because they got tired of chasing achievements or simply decided they didn’t want to keep going. That left me at 9 million Gamerscore with a real shot at becoming the first person to reach 10 million. That’s when I really started pushing for it.
When XBOX 360 launched, the idea of anyone ever reaching 10 million Gamerscore was almost unthinkable. But I don’t have another milestone in mind now. For me, the goal has always been to play, have fun, and do what I enjoy.
“When I start a game, I see it through to the end, at least when it comes to the original achievement list. I’ve been doing that for more than 10 years.”
Looking back on your achievement journey, which one was the hardest to unlock?
Siegfried: For me difficulty comes down on how much time something takes. Some achievements can be incredibly time-consuming, and Monster Hunter: World is a great example.
Getting every gold crown in Monster Hunter: World for the Giant Crown Master achievement was one of the toughest things I’ve ever done. It can be really frustrating to play for one, two, or even three days without making any progress because so much of it comes down to luck and getting the right monsters appear. It makes you want to cry and give up. [Laughs]

pool.titulo: AI kills another coding competition: 'I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models'
pool.resumen: After eight years of operation, the Atari Homebrew Awards are no more.
pool.contenido:
The Atari Homebrew Awards , an annual celebration of new games developed for old systems by the people who love them both, has been cancelled after eight years of operation—and yes, it's because of AI.
"As you may know, the landscape of retro game development changed dramatically this year with the massively increased capabilities of LLMs. More and more games have incorporated AI elements into their development chain and now have the capability to create full games without writing a single line of code," Atari Homebrew Awards host James, aka ZeroPage Homebrew, wrote on the Atari Age forums .
"Keeping up with the large number of AI-assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on, with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI. This flood of new AI games forced me to re-evaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.
"The Atari Homebrew Awards were now challenged to make sure the work of human developers were still honoured amongst the new fully computer-coded games. I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I quickly discovered that this was going to be more difficult than I thought."
James said he discovered last week that "a large majority" of developers were using AI in some capacity to make their games, from testing to wholesale game creation, "without one typed line of code." That left two options: Disallow any and all AI usage in the Atari Homebrew Awards competition, which James said would disqualify a large number of "extremely talented coders" who used AI in some very minor way, or let it slide and choose some sort of arbitrary dividing line between what is and isn't allowed—or just let it go entirely and allow everything, including fully vibe-coded games.
James said he wasn't interested in that, which meant he needed to settle on how much AI usage would be allowable—and also how to determine if AI was used at all, since some developers are better at disclosure than others. That, naturally, led to the worry that developers could be subject to "false positives and possible witch hunts," something that's already a problem in mainstream game development.
This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year.
ZeroPage Homebrew, Atari Homebrew Awards host
Ultimately, James decided there was no practical way forward, although he did leave open the possibility of a return someday. "This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year," he wrote. "I know many others feel the same way and I hope to be able to continue this tradition in the coming years as things settle into a new normal."
As we noted in July, debates over "acceptable" levels of AI use are cropping up all over the open source development scene : Some are drawing hard lines against it for principled and/or practical reasons, yet its popularity is growing explosively because, frankly, you don't need to know what you're doing in order to do it—as long as you're not too concerned with doing it well.
The Atari Homebrew Awards isn't the first such event to fall victim to the AI flood. Earlier in November, the Australian STEM Videogame Challenge, a "free national videogame development competition for students," announced that the 2026 event will be its last because "the rapid and complex rise of generative AI in game development [made] it harder to judge what students made themselves," and thus undercut the whole purpose of the program: Encouraging kids to learn how to code.

pool.titulo: Someone counted all 5,588 buildings in GTA 6, and it turns out you can go inside 28% of them
pool.resumen: Maybe even more will open up for Online, too.
pool.contenido:
Grand Theft Auto 6 hasn't even been out for a week yet, and someone has already done the math on how many buildings in the whole of Leonida you can actually walk into. For those of you who are curious: it's 1,563 buildings.
That is frankly ridiculous. I don't think I've ever been inside 1,563 different buildings in my entire life, although I am a creature of habit, so that could explain things. The player who shared these stats, Aileos , does note that there are 5,588 buildings in total, so the enterable buildings only account for a fraction of that, just over 25%.
There are some who will look at this with a glass-half-empty perspective, and I get it. This world is so cool, it's easy to want more of it, but as another player points out , "This would've sent us into psychosis a few years back". Sometimes it's better to focus on what we have rather than what we don't have. After all, how many buildings will you realistically enter in your GTA 6 playthrough? Probably not 1,563.
We've spent the past week here in the PC Gamer Slack channel marvelling at just how many random encounters you can stumble across in GTA 6. Some of us have found sentient NPCs. One of us was actually recognised by a convenience store clerk who then asked to get robbed, and I think we've all seen videos of the furry rescue mission.
But just because this world already has loads of awesome activities, it doesn't mean we aren't hoping for more. A massive casino and go-kart track have been spotted by players, both of which have huge "Coming Soon" signs draped outside of them.
These buildings could be lying in wait for GTA 6 Online, or they could be added to singleplayer sometime in the future. Regardless, those are two more buildings that will potentially welcome players soon.

pool.titulo: How to steal the Pegassi Infernus in GTA 6
pool.resumen: Pilfer the '96 Infernus from the police lockup for Randy.
pool.contenido:
Stealing the Pegassi Infernus in GTA 6 can be quite tricky, considering it's being held in the police department lockup, the building to the west of the police station in southwest Crosstown.
You can access the building via a yellow window cleaning elevator on the southern side of the building. But this won't appear until Randy texts and gives you the Infernus's location. If you go here before, your options for entering are far more limited and risky, so it's worth waiting. To get to the car:
Use the elevator to get inside. Turn right, then left, and make your way up to the seventh level of the multi-story car park—the purple Pegassi Infernus is easy to recognise since it's the only sports car in there. Select the key cloning option to get inside. Now you just need to drive down a few levels to exit via the police station parking lot—which I'd recommend—or keep going all the way down to exit at the bottom of the car park. Remember, you need to drive fast to stop the tracker going off, and if you hear it beeping, you should speed up to prevent it pinging the cops.
If you do bash around the car a bit, you can get it repaired at a gas station on the way. Bring it back in pristine condition and you'll net 15k for the trouble.

pool.titulo: Blade Runner 2099 Showrunner Explains the References to Philip K. Dick's Novel, Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep
pool.resumen: Silka Luisa, the creator, executive producer, and showrunner of Blade Runner 2099, explained why this series was the first entry in the franchise to include certain references from Philip K. Dick’s original novel.
pool.contenido:
Silka Luisa, the creator, executive producer, and showrunner of Blade Runner 2099, recently explained to IGN why this series was the first entry in the franchise to include certain references to Philip K. Dick’s original novel.
Warning: MAJOR spoilers for Blade Runner 2099 ahead! Turn back now if you haven’t watched the show!
Philip K. Dick’s genre-defining sci-fi novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? is the basis upon which Ridley Scott built the first Blade Runner movie back in 1982. It certainly had its differences from the source material — though Dick himself praised a television preview he saw just before his death — and was notably lacking a few central elements from the book, chief among them the empathy box and Deckard’s hand-wringing over a vanity purchase of an actual, real-life animal (hence the book’s title).
Near the beginning of the book, Deckard is in knots about keeping up with the Joneses; in the novel’s post-war future where global conditions have been extremely averse to almost all forms of life, animals are a rarity, and owning one is a luxury. Deckard and his wife — to whom he appears to harbor relative indifference, if not annoyance — own an electric sheep, which they keep on the rooftop of their apartment building.
Unable to stand the constraints of his financial class, he decides to purchase a black Nubian goat, which he hesitantly shows to his wife, who predictably blows up at him for making such a massive purchase without consulting her. She eventually comes around to the animal after actually setting eyes on it, however. (Eventually, the goat is killed by Rachael, a replicant with whom Deckard has an affair.) While this specific storyline isn’t in the original movie nor any subsequent Blade Runner media, a black goat does appear in Silka’s show.
This goat makes its appearance on the sea cliffs near Cora and Elias’s childhood home, which is where they lived with their adoptive mother, Helena. As Cora later comes to discover, Helena was one of the very first replicants ever made, a Nexus 1, created without a set lifespan and essentially immortal (as long as they can void injury or accidents). It’s a lovely parallel with the book as the goat represented Deckard’s desperation to cling to his humanity and his status in society. Helena was also a way for Cora to cling to her own humanity in a world run by replicants. But after learning that her mother was a Nexus 1, this illusion crashes down on her, much like the goat after it was pushed off the roof of Deckard’s apartment building by his scorned replicant lover.
Also included for the first time is the empathy box, a technological marvel that allows users to mentally and physically "feel" the events of whatever they are seeing on a screen in front of them. In this case, it’s Wilbur Mercer, a religious figure whose laborious climb up a mountain while being pelted with rocks has become a central part of a religion aptly named "Mercerism." In the book, the footage is discovered to be fake, having been filmed on a sound stage; Mercer was merely a character played by an actor named Al Jarry.
The empathy box shows up in one of the final episodes of Blade Runner 2099. A Mercerite forces the dying replicant Olwen to use the box, where she watches Mercer climb the mountain and feels herself being pelted with stones.
I asked Silka about these references and why she felt they were important to include in the show when previous adaptations had largely ignored them in favor of building upon Scott’s specific version of Dick’s literary world.
“I mean, Philip K. Dick is a genius,” Silka told me. “His book is so prescient. I think what's so special about him and his writing is not just that he was able to look into the future and really see not only what would happen, but the dangers of what would happen, but he also has a way of doing it where it's this playful, zany tone that you almost... It doesn't leave you with a feeling of dread, but the ideas are very, very dark. And the juxtaposition of those two things, this playful tone plus these dark ideas, that felt like a direction and a north star, tonally, for us to pursue.
“And also just as a lover of the book, I love Mercerism. I was so curious as to, ‘Okay, what would an empathy box look like? Who were the practitioners? What did Wilbur's climb actually look like?’ So much of that had lived in my imagination. And so then, to be able to actually sit with people and say, ‘Well, what do you think it looks like?’ And then look at references and build that out, it was really exciting."
I mentioned to Silka that I had paused the show to check my own copy of the book, just to make sure I wasn’t hallucinating that I remembered something about a guy climbing a mountain and getting hit with a bunch of rocks. It actually made me re-read the novel, which, in turn, gave me a much greater appreciation for the series. (Silka also mentioned that the show boasts a few additional references to Dick’s short stories; a girl’s toy robot named "My Lord" is one of these.)
“That’s what I hope [happens],” an enthusiastic Silka replied. “Everyone should read it.”
Blade Runner 2099 is available to steam on Prime Video. For more news about the show, check out my interview with Alcon Entertainment co-CEOs Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, as well as IGN’s review of this latest entry in the Blade Runner franchise.

pool.titulo: 'It's Such a Shame' — Blade Runner 2099's Lewis Gribben Mourns EA's Closure of BioWare
pool.resumen: I got the chance to sit down with the supporting cast of Blade Runner 2099, and naturally, we started chatting about video games. I had to ask about their favorite games, to which Lewis Gribben gave a topical answer involving the now-shuttered BioWare.
pool.contenido:
I got the chance to sit down with the supporting cast of Blade Runner 2099, and naturally, we started chatting about video games. I had to ask about their favorite games, to which Lewis Gribben gave a topical answer involving the now-shuttered BioWare.
BioWare — the Canadian game studio behind hit AAA RPGs like Dragon Age and Mass Effect — was closed by EA in October , sparking outrage among fans and those within the industry itself. The knife twisted further when a former BioWare employee leaked a trailer for the next Mass Effect game , which, by all accounts, looked extremely ambitious and well in the middle of production. (EA decided to cancel the project rather than move it to a different development team or sell it off to another studio.)
Lewis Gribben, who plays Elias opposite Hunter Schafer’s Cora in Blade Runner 2099, gushed about the Mass Effect series and mourned the loss of BioWare, while also making sure to float his name for a possible role in Amazon’s TV adaptation of the games.
“There’s so many [games] that I could mention, but the franchise that I think is one of the best sci-fi franchises is Mass Effect,” Gribben told me. “I think it’s so good. I think it’s such an amazing and incredible world. I know Amazon is considering making a TV show of it. Please, think about me for it.
“I think it’s so good, and I think it’s such a shame that BioWare shut down recently and that studio is no longer gonna exist, but they were so great at telling epic stories and you getting to choose how you shape your character, good or bad, and I think that adjacent to being a franchise and a sci-fi world is what makes the franchise so amazing.”
Dimitri Abold, who plays the character Bebeto, said his favorite game is Final Fantasy 7 , and that he’s looking forward to the next installment in the remake trilogy next year. Matthew Needham, who plays the replicant named Yahya, revealed that he started playing video games during the pandemic with The Last of Us — which he joked was probably not the best pick during a global virus, though we all agreed that it was a standout game and a good choice for someone just getting into gaming.
Following up on this question, I revealed a tidbit from my conversation with Alcon Entertainment co-CEOs Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, who told me that they have had talks about adapting Blade Runner into a AAA video game . All three actors seemed excited by the idea and said they were game to be part of the project, if it ever comes to fruition.
“It would be really cool,” Gribben said. “We could kind of connect the TV show with the game.”
“That’d be so sick,” Abold remarked excitedly, to which Needham replied, “That’d be fun.”
Blade Runner 2099 is available to stream on Prime Video. For more news about the series, check out IGN’s review , as well as our explainer for its ending in case you had a few remaining questions after watching.

pool.titulo: Both Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade & Rebirth Are at All-Time Low Black Friday Prices On Switch 2
pool.resumen: Amazon's Black Friday deals have dropped Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade and Rebirth to record-low prices on Nintendo Switch 2, saving you up to 37%
pool.contenido:
Any Nintendo Switch 2 owners who’ve been keen to catch up on the last two Final Fantasy 7 games in the Remake trilogy before FF7 Revelation can now grab both physical games for under £50, thanks to a surprise couple of big Black Friday deals.
At Amazon UK right now, you can buy the game card Nintendo Switch 2 ports of Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade for only £22.95 (normally £27.95) and Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth for just £25 (brought down by 37% from £39.95).
Save Big On Final Fantasy 7 Remake Titles For Switch 2 Those are not only the lowest prices we've seen for both boxed games on Amazon yet (confirmed by us at IGN UK), but this Switch 2 version of FF7 Rebirth is also the previously limited edition with the exclusive ‘Zack Fair’ Magic: The Gathering card .
As for FF7 Remake, the Intergrade version you get with the Switch 2 port is essentially the ‘Complete Edition’ of the game: adding performance improvements, a photo mode, a new superboss, an extra difficulty setting, and — most importantly — the Episode INTERmission story DLC featuring Yuffie Kisaragi.
To clarify, however, whilst these are both indeed physical versions of the two Final Fantasy 7 Remake games, the game cartridges supplied in the case are Game-Key Cards — meaning no game data is kept on each card, and needs to be entirely downloaded to your Nintendo Switch 2 console via the internet.
So, you’ll need to be sure your internal storage has enough space for either or both games as you play: the file sizes being 90.4GB for Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade and 91.5 GB for Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth .
That said, to reiterate, Game-Key Cards are still reusable items and are a step-up from digital games shipped as a code in a box, such as GTA 6 skipping a disc release to be a purely digital-only game . As they still come in the form of physical cartridges, you will still be able to later resell, trade in, or lend out your copies of FF7 Remake Intergrade and Rebirth after you’ve finished playing them — if you so wish.

pool.titulo: Fan-Made GTA 5 Port for iPhone Shuts Down After Take-Two Cease and Desist
pool.resumen: A cease and desist from Rockstar parent company Take-Two has put an end to a fan-made port of GTA 5 for Apple devices a month after the creator went public with it.
pool.contenido:
A cease and desist from Rockstar parent company Take-Two has put an end to a fan-made port of GTA 5 for Apple devices a month after the creator went public with it.
Five Star Port launched in October this year as a full native port that ran locally on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. On newer hardware like the A20 Pro chip, the port boasted frame rates between 40 and 60fps at near-native resolution and max graphics settings. It also supported foldable phones, with the controllers and map appearing on the lower portion and the game on the upper portion of the screen.
Kevin, the creator of the port, posted a farewell message to the unofficial port’s website . “GTA V has always been one of my favorite games,” he said. “I've made mods for it, worked with FiveM, managed and hosted FiveM servers, and played on plenty of others. It has given me a lot of great memories. Getting to bring it to people who don't have a PC or a console, so they could play it on a phone, has been really, really cool. I honestly never thought this game could run on a phone at all.
“Take-Two Interactive, through their lawyers, has sent me a cease and desist asking me to stop all activity under the Five Star Port name and everything related to it. I am complying with it.”
Five Star Port’s website, app, and online services were shut down immediately. The Telegram and Discord groups have been made read-only and will be deleted on November 27.
“I'm not involved in and don't endorse any continuation, rebrand or copy of the port, and I can't help with files or links,” Kevin added. He also posted a warning that scammers have been passing around copies of the port, claiming to have a “new version” of it. These could spread computer viruses.
“Thank you again to everyone who supported this project: everyone who playtested, everyone who sent suggestions and feedback, and everyone who helped make it a great port that is actually fully playable on an iPhone,” Kevin signed off. “That still feels wild to me.”
Take-Two has a history of forcing fan projects offline, so perhaps it comes as no surprise to see Five Star Port fall by the wayside. The company is currently battling homebrew efforts to vibecode a PC port of GTA 6 , which some believe is mere days away from being playable.

If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . pool.titulo: GTA 6: Here's Why You Should Go Back to Jason's House After Chapter 1
pool.resumen: Here’s why you should go back to Jason’s house after chapter 1 of GTA 6.
pool.contenido:
Warning: spoilers for Chapter 1 of GTA 6 follow.
If you’ve played through chapter one of GTA 6, you’ll know that Jason’s home isn’t in the best of shape following its final mission. On fire, and certainly no place to raise a child, the crib, coffee table, and all of your chosen home improvements are left either shattered or cindered by the time Lucia escapes, taking with her only one valuable: a photo of the couple’s son, Tomás. But not all is lost, and it’s worth going back to check what remains.
From the beginning of chapter two onward, going back to Jason’s waterside house can be a risky move to make. Flick open the map, and you’ll see a red area surrounding his immediate neighbourhood that signifies a police presence in the area. Of course, you’re free to head back straight away, but you’ll see a few cop cars sat outside his home, with a few people waiting in case you do return to the scene of the crime. Sneak past them if you trust your stealth skills, or opt for a much quicker and violent smash-and-grab maneuver if that’s more your style.
If you're patient, though, that heat will eventually diminish over the course of the story, so you can walk straight through the front door. I’m not exactly sure if that’s tied to your progress through GTA 6’s main missions, or the in-game clock itself, but I can confirm that from around halfway through chapter three, that red zone had disappeared for me.
Once inside the ashen remains of Jason’s former quiet life, there are a couple of items of note to grab hold of. Both of these can be found under the floorboards of the bedroom where Jason’s stash once lay hidden. While you won’t be able to recover all of the money you stored there before realising it would be gone forever — I guess it burned, whereas the metal tin next to it protected its contents — you can find both his personal collection of photos and a rainy day fund worth $5,000.
The former is a nice extra wrinkle to the story, as Jason and Lucia will make sure to cherish these photos, alongside the one she recovered of Tommy, and carry them with them from home to home around Leonida on their nomadic adventures. The latter is no small amount when starting again from scratch at the outset of chapter two, which does make the risk of getting busted worth it to get a head start in Port Gellhorn. Wait until chapter three, as I did, and that amount of money makes less of a difference.
But that isn’t all. When Lucia grapples with the two masked men who set the home on fire, Jason’s pet snake, Dolores, makes a daring escape when her glass enclosure is smashed. We saw her head for the door, but are left wondering whether she managed to dance through the flames to safety. Well, when returning to the home, make sure to check under the back steps, where you can find our serpentine friend alive and well. And she’s not alone either. Get a closer look to find her curled up around some eggs, signalling a whole host of mini Dolores’s are on the way. Perhaps they’ll rebuild this home together, and turn the whole of Key Lento into a snake town over time. Far-fetched, perhaps, but have you seen some of the bonkers sh*t happening in this game?
It’s just one example of how Rockstar has managed to build out the world of GTA 6 so successfully, making it feel like a place that carries on living even when you’re not there. This sort of thing is littered throughout Leonida as you progress through the story and the passing of time takes effect. Road and building works that start out as mounds of dirt slowly become more developed as chapters go by, with pipes being laid down and bricks stacked.
And Jason’s house isn’t the only place he and Lucia call home that’s worth revisiting long after they’ve departed. The Startlet Motel from chapter two also changes, offering new gameplay and story opportunities. GTA 6 is a game that rewards curiosity, often answering your questions with a satisfying answer, and returning to Jason’s home is just one example of it.

pool.titulo: The Outrage Over Jason Buying Lucia Flowers Is GTA 6's Dumbest Controversy
pool.resumen: Some corners of the internet are furious Rockstar has apparently turned its crime simulator into a game about being a considerate boyfriend, while others are discovering that Jason Duval might just be the perfect man.
pool.contenido:
Of all the things I expected Grand Theft Auto 6 to cause arguments about, whether or not a man should buy his girlfriend flowers was pretty low on the list. Yet some corners of the internet are furious that Rockstar has apparently turned its crime simulator into a game about being a considerate boyfriend, while others are discovering that Jason Duval might just be the perfect man – a sentence I never thought I’d write about a Grand Theft Auto protagonist.
As well as the usual GTA activities of stealing cars, shooting people, and generally being a menace to society, GTA 6 gives players the option to nurture the relationship between its two protagonists, Jason and Lucia. It's especially prevalent at the start of the game, where you can renovate their home, buy Lucia flowers, pick out clothes and accessories for her while shopping, bring her drinks, open car doors, and even hold her hand while walking around Leonida. I think it's all rather sweet, especially when you consider that these two are also quite happy to commit armed robberies together. Couples who crime together, stay together. (That's not a spoiler; that's me high on hopium as I play through the story.)
Crucially, all of this romantic housekeeping is optional. The game certainly prompts you to nurture the relationship, especially early on when we're just finding out who Jason and Lucia are. But when the button-press to hold hands or show affection pops up, you're free to ignore it. Over time, this will cause the relationship to cool to the point where eventually they become platonic partners in crime, but they're still very much in it together.
Showing affection is also not specific to Jason either – once you're through chapter one, which is heavily focussed on the army vet, and deeper into the game where you spend more time as both characters, they can both choose to show the other affection – or not, if you so desire. You choose how much effort they want to put into Jason and Lucia’s relationship, and the game responds accordingly. You can make them the sort of disgustingly loved-up couple who make everyone around them feel slightly ill, or let their relationship cool into something more businesslike. No-one is being forced to play house.
From a quick browse of social media, and, in particular, X, you'll see posts reading "RIP GTA. Killed by women. Like so many before," from @trackthedecline. User @ExoGhost writes, "GTA 6 has a mission where you need to buy flowers for Lucia. This game is such woke slop. It's so obvious it was made by women". And then there's @5jmxgz, who claims, "gta 6 lowk the biggest flop ever, we waited 13 years for a literal cuck simulator."
Grand Theft Auto 6 cemented itself as the most successful entertainment launch of all-time, making $3.79 billion in just one day.
For some players, the problem seems to be that they’ve waited 13 years for a new GTA game, only to find themselves assembling furniture and picking up groceries. There’s a reasonable argument buried somewhere in there about whether mundane domestic activities are what people want from a series built on criminal excess and absolute freedom. If you spend your actual life doing chores, perhaps coming home to do more of them in a video game isn’t particularly appealing? The pace of Chapter 1 feels like deliberate decision from Rockstar to subvert what people expect from GTA, and I think it's that that's causing at least some of the reaction, because once you move onto chapter 2 and beyond, the only chores you're really doing is putting cups in the sink, opening car doors, and getting your significant other a snack now and again. No one is cleaning the oven or pulling lint out of the dryer.
However, some of the complaints go considerably further, treating the idea of Jason showing any kind of affection or consideration for Lucia as an attack on masculinity itself. Some have described the game as a “cuck simulator” while reacting to Jason running errands for Lucia. Apparently buying your girlfriend something nice is now a threat to civilization. Someone should probably warn the florists.
For me, GTA 6 is Rockstar at its subversive best. While internet conflict raged over whether or not games were getting too “woke” and that the heroes were becoming too “soft,” Rockstar gave us a strong, straight, masculine guy with a hot girlfriend. The only catch? You have to put in the work that goes with that. You need to put effort into the relationship to keep the hot girlfriend, you need to go to the gym to stay buff, you need to contribute to the household finances.
Some X users are seeing the positives in Jason and Lucia's dynamic, and the warmth shared between them. "When he said 'you and Tommy are the only family I need', then went ahead to include her mom because he knows how important she is to her. Yep Jason Duval is not just a green flag but the greenest forest," says @keiuzuki. It's a sentiment shared by many others, who are already creating collages, montages, and memes dedicated to Mr Duval.
For plenty of female players, Jason’s appeal isn’t just that he’s attractive, capable, or willing to commit a little light felony in the name of love. It’s that he pays attention. He notices things. He makes an effort. And while the bar for romantic male behavior probably shouldn’t be somewhere around buying flowers and remembering to open a car door, there’s something undeniably appealing about a game that makes those little gestures feel important. The man has a criminal record, questionable career prospects, and presumably several outstanding warrants, but at least he remembers to buy you a lemonade.
There’s also a particularly funny subset of women watching their real-life partners enthusiastically renovate a fictional house, buy fictional flowers, and take their fictional girlfriend shopping, while wondering when exactly that energy might make its way into their actual relationship. pool.titulo: Cassette Beasts 2002 Preview: An Unmistakably British – and Impressive – Creature-Collecting RPG
pool.resumen: After playing through Cassette Beasts 2002’s opening hours for this preview, I kept playing. While I can’t talk about what I’ve seen since wrapping up the first chunk of my adventure, its opening hours made a strong first impression. I’m charmed by Bytten Studio’s beast design, writing, and distinct take on the creature-collecting RPG. It’s scratching the catch-n-battle itch I get this time of year, and I don’t see that changing anytime soon.
pool.contenido:
Key Preview Takeaways:
I'm charmed by the beast design, writing, and distinct take on the creature-collecting RPG. The battle system builds nicely off of what I loved in Pokemon and Persona. It is unmistakably British in a really fun way. After playing through Cassette Beasts 2002’s opening hours for this preview, I kept playing. While I can’t talk about what I’ve seen since wrapping up the first chunk of my adventure, its opening hours made a strong first impression. I’m charmed by Bytten Studio’s beast design, writing, and distinct take on the creature-collecting RPG. It’s scratching the catch-n-battle itch I get this time of year, and I don’t see that changing anytime soon.
Lately, I’ve been glued to an online battle simulator from another creature collecting RPG series. Just hopelessly hooked. So when a game like Cassette Beasts gives me an opportunity to stop tugging at the slot machine arm of randomized browser-bound battle teams and build one, I turn my head and pay attention.
Cassette Beasts 2002 made the most of my embattled attention span. Its battle system takes a lot of what I love about Pokemon and Persona and goes a little deeper on some of the ideas that drive the rock-paper-scissors type advantages. For example, water-based attacks will rust metal, weakening metallic Beasts’ defenses. Some attacks might cause Resonance on a metal creature, which automatically knocks it out once enough stacks build up.
Water-based attacks will rust metal, weakening metallic Beasts’ defenses. I love this approach to type advantages, which capitalizes on strategy in a cool way. The fact that I can just stack Resonance a few times creates a mini-objective in battle that goes beyond just finding the best type advantage. Chasing these objectives adds a lot more depth to this style of turn-based combat that I absolutely adore.
So does the Fusion system, which lets any two Beasts combine into one powerful critter. This is one of the most impressive mechanics I’ve seen in this kind of game. I’m no mathematician, but with over 200 Beasts on the roster (more than 120 are new, by the way), that leaves room for a staggering number of different combinations. While I only saw a small handful of the available Fusions, these super-powered Beasts gain four action points each turn to spend on special moves and abilities in battle, rather than the standard two.
Set in 2000’s London, Cassette Beasts 2002 is unmistakably British. As an American who hasn’t been to the United Kingdom, I’m positive some cultural references and quips have flown over my head, but I still caught a few. For example, the first area in the dream world occupied by the eponymous tape critters (Nodol) is called Bethnal Blue, rather than Bethnal Green.
Naturally, my understanding starts and ends with knowing these names, so I can’t really speak to the actual location or twist Cassette Beasts 2002 is trying to bring to it. Still, that nod to an East London neighborhood feels at home next to references to the works of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle and The Bard. Recent news has me holding out for a Fleming nod.
The world Cassette Beasts 2002 occupies feels as alive as it does tuned to its time and place. Through the course of my demo, I made friends with the locals, bought coffee from the local convenience store worker, and met my exhausted, drink-slinging counterpart across the pond. Brought to life by charming writing and talented voice acting, each character felt believable and interesting enough to actually stop and talk to.
Walking around town reminded me of going outside in my own neighborhood and bumping into a neighbor or bar regular. Maybe this was all canned stuff, designed to fill out and flatter the first part of the game, but the skill trees I saw for some of my digital neighbors suggest otherwise.
Walking around town reminded me of going outside in my own neighborhood and bumping into a neighbor or bar regular. Completing sidequests in Nodol, searching in the right places, or progressing in the story will net you Seeds of Inspiration, which you use to fill out the nodes on these NPCs’ skill trees. Each tree represents something different. The shopkeeper’s path gates off helpful items like better healing for your Beasts, whereas my new friend Sai’s skill tree offers upgrades that improve both his skills in battle and helpful upgrades to things like the buffs gained from eating food in-battle.
It would be silly to talk about a game called Cassette Beasts in which you literally record the creatures you’re capturing without mentioning its soundtrack. I heard roughly an EP’s worth of music across the three-hour demo. It’s a small sample size for what’s probably going to be a 20-ish-hour game if the previous Cassette Beasts’ HowLongToBeat page is any indication, but it left a good impression. My favorite stuff showed up in boss fights against foes like Copskin, but the overworld theme for Bethnal Blue was as chill as the snow-capped mountains. I’m sure the best stuff is reserved for late-game boss fights.
Cassette Beasts 2002 promises a nostalgic trip to an era of tape decks and payphones. Built on a clever, distinct battle system that goes beyond just rock, paper, scissors and set in a charming, lived-in world, I’ll probably keep my Steam Deck nearby for a few days to come. It’s slated for release in March of next year, so it’ll be a while before you can get your hands on this one. But it’s just as well; you’re probably going to be pretty busy with another game in which the soundtrack is heavily emphasized for the next few months.

pool.titulo: The Witcher 4 and All CD Projekt's Upcoming Games Remain Multiplatform Despite PlayStation Marketing Deal, CD Projekt Boss Reassures
pool.resumen: CD Projekt co-CEO Michał Nowakowski has reassured fans that The Witcher 4 remains a multiplatform game despite its PlayStation marketing deal with Sony.
pool.contenido:
CD Projekt co-CEO Michał Nowakowski has reassured fans that The Witcher 4 remains a multiplatform game despite its PlayStation marketing deal with Sony.
Announced yesterday as part of CD Projekt’s latest financial results , the partnership with Sony Interactive Entertainment also covers its games on PlayStation and PlayStation Plus. CD Projekt said the deal “will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years.”
While the terms of the deal remain undisclosed, it is expected that The Witcher 4 marketing will feature PS5 prominently, perhaps even exclusively, as GTA 6’s marketing has done with the “Plays Best on PS5” tagline.
In a follow-up post on social media , Nowakowski insisted The Witcher 4, which is slated for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X and S, remains a multiplatform release, as do all the games CD Projekt has in the works. That presumably means no exclusivity deal for Cyberpunk 2, not that anyone suspected one might be put in place.
“We’re looking forward to our partnership with PlayStation! And just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform,” Nowakowski said.
Already there is concern around The Witcher 4’s PlayStation marketing deal, following the debate around GTA 6’s “Plays Best on PS5” tagline. As we’ve reported, the Xbox Series X version of Rockstar’s epic has better performance than the PS5 version , which has caused some to say they feel misled.
The Witcher 4 isn’t due out until 2028 so there’s a long time to go before we see the result of CD Projekt’s effort, but marketing is expected to ramp up significantly in the coming months. Excitement is building, and this week CD Projekt said it expects the leap between The Witcher 3 and 4 to be comparable to the one between GTA 5 and 6 .
As of October 31, 2026, CD Projekt had 513 staff working on The Witcher 4, which is actually down slightly on the previous number reported three months earlier. The number of people working on Cyberpunk 2, however, has ramped up, from 184 to 199.
CD Projekt has a huge amount going on right now. The Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, launches next year, followed by The Witcher 4 in 2028. CD Projekt has an ambitious plan to release further The Witcher sequels hot on the heels of The Witcher 4 as part of a new trilogy of games. Then there’s Cyberpunk 2 to squeeze in there at some point, The Witcher remake, Project Hadar, and Project Sirius.

pool.titulo: Hershey Chocolate Bars Drop Back Down to Their Original Price of 5 Cents for Today Only
pool.contenido:
The Hershey movie just opened in theaters, and of course that’s cause for some chocolate festivities. We happen to be in the thick of Black Friday deals , so what better way to celebrate than with a solid discount?
Well, Hershey is taking discounts to a whole new level. For today only, 5oz Hershey chocolate bars have dropped to their retail price from the year 1900: five cents. For reference, in 2026, the chocolate bars typically retail for around $2.
Don’t expect to see the 5-cent Hershey bar everywhere you look - only Amazon, Walmart, and select Hershey store locations are participating in the deal. The Amazon discount went live at 9am EST and will theoretically go away at 9pm EST, unless the retailer decides to offer a little Black Friday treat.
If you’re a real chocoholic, you might as well stock up for the foreseeable future.
Where to Buy 5-Cent Hershey Bars - Today Only
Amazon Grocery, which offers same-day delivery, is your best bet for getting the chocolate deal. You can also find the standard Hershey bar discount through Walmart.
Chocolate bars in exclusive vintage packaging are being handed out at two Hershey store locations : the official Hershey location, of course, and the store in Times Square. Hershey notes that the special edition bars available in stores are limited to 10 per person.
The Hershey movie , meanwhile, is now showing in select theaters. It follows Milton Hershey, played by Finn Wittrock, as he builds the chocolate empire we now all know and love.
While the company itself was founded in its initial form in 1897, Hershey didn’t debut the iconic milk chocolate bar until 1900. The bar was launched at the price of a nickel, and its affordability is now considered a major contributing factor to the company’s lasting success. What better way to appreciate the history of the chocolate company than to experience it?

pool.titulo: Blade Runner 2099 Ending Explained and Biggest Burning Questions
pool.resumen: Blade Runner 2099 ending explained and burning questions: We break down the details on the latest addition to the future noir sci-fi franchise.
pool.contenido:
This article contains spoilers for the full season of Blade Runner 2099 on Prime Video.
After eight episodes of Hunter Schafer doing the “ don’t be suspicious ” scene from Parks and Recreation, Blade Runner 2099 has run its last blades. And as with Blade Runner and Blade Runner 2049 before it, the TV series is being awfully mysterious with what exactly is going on at the end — perhaps even more mysterious, given the multiple open questions about not just the main characters of the show but also what will happen to the world of Blade Runner following these game-changing events.
More: Blade Runner 2099 Review
Are we being mysterious? Perhaps. But we’re going to try and sift through some of those bigger questions and attempt to provide some answers here before these moments are lost in time, like tears in rain.
Blade Runner 2099 Ending Explained First, let’s recap to distill the rather complex plot of all eight episodes. One thing to emphasize is that just like Blade Runner and Blade Runner 2049 before it, the conclusion of the series is less about neatly wrapping up the plot than moving the main characters from one emotional place to another. Here, those main characters are Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), an aging Replicant who has a few days left until she dies, and Cora (Schafer), a human pretending to be a Replicant in order to find a memory her adoptive mother gifted her back when she was young.
As we head into the finale, “Share The Fantasy,” Olwen has realized that she wants more time to live, while Cora is laser-focused on getting that memory back. Cora also now knows that her (non-biological) “mother” Helena (Sheila Atim) was a Replicant… and not just any Replicant, but a Nexus-1 — aka the very first prototype version created by the Tyrell Corporation way back in the late 1990s and released in the year 2000*.
(*In case that’s confusing, since you probably don’t remember Replicants wandering around in the real world, the original movie took place in the at-the-time far future of 2019.)
Helena, Cora has discovered, was killed by Julius (Tom Burke), the other surviving Nexus-1, who has been looking for the aforementioned memory. That memory belongs to none other than Eldon Tyrell himself (Joe Turkel in the original movie, though at least in part since he passed away in 2022; he doesn’t appear in any form in the series other than a brief glimpse from the back), giving Julius the key to creating more Nexus-1 replicants.
Cora and Olwen arrive at a Tyrell Off-World Launch complex, get in a big fight with a bunch of Julius’ acolytes — including a resurrected Clotilde (Amy Lennox), now a Nexus-1 — and ultimately kill Julius after he’s already destroyed the memory. In the process, Olwen is injured, and it sure looks like Cora is killed (more on that in a second)... that is, until Clotilde, who Olwen saved from death, explains that she also knows the Nexus-1 process.
We see someone get turned into a Nexus-1, though it’s not clear who. Our two main characters end their storyline with Olwen now off-world exploring other planets — possibly watching C-beams glitter near the Tannhäuser Gate, but that’s not specified — while Cora returns to the Replicant police station and is given the formerly Replicant and now human-detecting Voight-Kampff test by the young Greta (Katelyn Rose Downey). She fails the test, though something is different about her. Maybe it’s her hair? Yeah, probably her hair.
Whew, that’s a lot! But there are a lot of other characters to get into, other plot points to discuss, and even some bigger world ramifications for where this could go next in Blade Runner 3019 or whatever is next. So let’s get to some burning questions and answer them however we can.
Is Cora a Replicant? This is always going to be the number one burning question with any Blade Runner property, with the original going both ways on whether Harrison Ford’s Rick Deckard is or isn’t a Replicant depending on which cut of the movie you watch and which film crew member you ask. Here, the huge honking question mark is over Cora’s head, as it sure looks like Julius kills her, based on the way Olwen is cradling her limp body.
Is there evidence against her being a Replicant? She fails the Voight-Kampff test and has a tear in her eye as she talks to Greta at the end of the finale. Also, the logistics of how a human would become a Replicant — taking her memories and putting them into a Nexus-1 body, perhaps? — raises even more questions.
Considering the enigmatic way Ridley Scott and Denis Villeneuve left Deckard, we think it’s pretty safe to declare that yes, Cora is now a Nexus-1. On the other hand? Olwen leaves the Off-World Launch complex without her, and she seems healthy and fine once she’s talking to Greta. Despite the test, she’s far more calm and calculated versus the raw emotion she displayed previously in the series. And why would Cora return to the police station at all if she’s human? Why put herself in more danger?
Obviously, this is straddling the line, so it’s entirely up to the viewer to decide if she’s a Replicant. But considering the enigmatic way Ridley Scott and Denis Villeneuve left Deckard, we think it’s pretty safe to declare that yes, Cora is now a Nexus-1. And if she is, that explains how she’s able to access her emotions more readily and fail the test, just like how Helena adopted two little humans and pretended to be their human mother for years.
Did Olwen Take the Nexus-1 Treatment? This is a little less clear, though the order of scenes and the fact that Olwen has repeatedly said she wants more time makes it probable that she was turned into a Nexus-1 then headed out into the stars to experience more worlds. It’s possible she left Cora’s dead body behind and had no idea she was about to get Nexus-a-fied; following that logic, Olwen went out into space to see one more beautiful thing before she died. But the more likely possibility is yes, she’s a Nexus-1.

pool.titulo: Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Let You Replay Missions–It Felt “Alien And Disconnected”
pool.resumen:
One of the first things people noticed with Grand Theft Auto 6 is that you cannot replay missions , at least not in a simple, straightforward way. GTA 5 had a mission replay option, as did Red Dead Redemption II, so why doesn't GTA 6?
Senior design director Scott Butchard told Kotaku that Rockstar "certainly" considered a mission replay feature "early on in development." However, Butchard said, "As the game came together, it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected."
He went on to say replaying missions "really diminished the choices you had made."
While GTA 6 doesn't make it easy to replay missions, you still can do so by reloading an earlier GTA 6 save. Something else to know is that if you're in the middle of a mission and it's not going to plan, you can open the game menu and select retry, quit, or restart.
GTA 6 blasted off with 32.5 million sales via prepurchases alone and around $4 billion in revenue on day one . The game is only going to get bigger and sell more copies over time, and it's helping drive new PlayStation and Xbox hardware sales .

Dying means losing half of the cinders you've collected, but they are also lost when the Helltide ends. Oftentimes that means having left over amounts of cinders you can't spend, only to then go to the next Helltide five minutes later and repeat the process from zero. It's been this way since Diablo 4 launched back in 2023.
In Season 16, that will finally change. Blizzard is getting rid of the downtime between Helltides spawning and making it so there will always be a Helltide up in one of the game's original zones, as well as one in expansion areas like Hahantu or Skovos. Even better, Aberrant Cinders won't be lost once a Helltide ends. Instead, players can collect up to 5,000 cinders at a time to be spent on opening chests within the activity. pool.titulo: Another Gaming Console Price Hike Could Be Coming, Thanks To New Tariffs
pool.resumen:
The US government has announced a new round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners. Under the proposed tariffs, import taxes will rise significantly, with China facing up to 40% when the new duties take effect next year. According to the BBC , some of the rates will be reduced because of tariff caps that US President Donald Trump has already agreed to, and individual countries could also face different levies.
What does this mean for gaming hardware? Trump's first round of "Liberation Day" tariffs contributed to rising console prices, but the Supreme Court eventually struck them down. Big companies like Sony , Microsoft, and Nintendo benefited from tariff refunds after the ruling, but they didn't pass the savings on to consumers. In Sony's case, it was estimated to get back $508 million in refunds from the US government.

pool.titulo: Lords Of The Fallen 2 Delayed Yet Again
pool.resumen:
CI Games has announced that Lords of the Fallen II is coming in April 2027, meaning it's been delayed again. An exact release date will be announced in December, the company said, and people are theorizing that could mean the date will be announced at The Game Awards on December 10.
Lords of the Fallen II was originally scheduled to launch in 2026, but CI Games delayed it to Q1 2027 (January-March) to avoid GTA 6 and give the team more time to polish the experience . Now it's delayed to Q2 2027.
For the previous delay, CI Games said feedback and tests showed that there are “meaningful opportunities” available to “further refine and strengthen the overall experience” with more time.
Despite its name, Lords of the Fallen 2 is actually the third game in the series, following Lord of the Fallen (2014) and Lords of the Fallen (2023).
Based in Poland, CI Games is also known for the Sniper: Ghost Warrior series, the latest entry being 2021's Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2.

pool.titulo: PS5 And Xbox Series X|S Console Sales Surged Just Before GTA 6 Came Out
pool.resumen:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and to play the game natively, you need a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S. Unsurprisingly, new data shows that PlayStation and Xbox console sales surged in the week before release.
According to Circana's Mat Piscatella , there was a "significant surge" in hardware sales in the US for the week that ended November 14. PS5 sales were >2.4x the same week last year, while Xbox Series X|S sales increased by >2.3x.
GTA 6 is not available on Switch 2, but that console saw a 40% surge in sales compared to the same week in 2025.
Before launch, Piscatella said GTA 6 should help boost PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales, but maybe not so dramatically due to the astronomical cost of a new console.
To help save money, you could buy an Xbox One and stream GTA 6 . Alternatively, people have discovered that you can stream the game to a PlayStation Portal device.
GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one.
For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of five things to do first.

pool.titulo: Is GTA 6 Too Easy? Rockstar Weighs In
pool.resumen:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and one of the things people are talking about is the game's difficulty level . Some are saying it's too easy. Rockstar boss Rob Nelson has now entered the conversation, telling Destructoid that Rockstar's data showed that GTA 4 was "a little too punishing in places" and GTA 5 was "perhaps too easy." So with GTA 6, the team trying to "land somewhere in the middle."
GTA 6 has no defined difficulty levels , which is in keeping with the franchise's tradition. That said, players can adjust things like aiming controls, while players can unlock cheat codes to make the game easier or harder.
Design producer Scott Mitchell, meanwhile, said the fail states in GTA 6 were designed to feel "appropriate."
“We wanted to keep things open and not limit the players’ use of mechanics, such as stealth, but we did also want to make sure we retained the cinematic, high production value, explosive sequences that we’re known for, and people expect. It feels like we’ve managed to strike a good balance," he explained.
Also in the interview, Nelson said figuring out the difficulty level for GTA 6 is itself challenging because the designers themselves know enemy positions

pool.resumen:

Netflix España la retira de su catálogo este jueves 26 de noviembre y no sé a qué hora exacta desaparecerá, así que lo más prudente es verla esta misma noche. Yo la volví a ver hace poco y me dio tanto miedo como la primera vez en el cine en su estreno en 1999. Desde entonces han pasado veintisiete años y un montón de pelis de terror con muchísimo más dinero que la han imitado. Y eso que su planteamiento no puede ser más sencillo: tres estudiantes de cine se meten en un bosque de Maryland para grabar un documental sobre una leyenda local y desaparecen. Lo que vemos es lo que grabaron.
Mucha gente se la creyó
Daniel Myrick y Eduardo Sánchez la rodaron en ocho días con unos 60.000 dólares , cuatro duros incluso para 1999, y dejaron que sus tres actores improvisaran buena parte de lo que se ve. Ni siquiera se cambiaron el nombre: Heather Donahue, Joshua Leonard y Michael C. Williams son Heather, Josh y Mike también en la ficción. Acabó recaudando unos 248 millones de dólares en todo el mundo.

Eso sí, el futuro Total War: Medieval 3 , que aún no tiene fecha de lanzamiento ni siquiera una ventana de estreno, tiene una tarea importantísima entre manos: tras varios vaivenes del estudio en lo que a diplomacia se refiere, los británicos quieren dar a la habilidad para cerrar tratos la importancia que se merece. Según han confirmado, ser un buen estratega militar no será suficiente para garantizar el éxito de nuestra campaña, y para ello se han fijado en uno de los juegos más queridos de la saga: Total War: Three Kingdoms .
Como mencionábamos, la diplomacia siempre ha sido uno de los aspectos más irregulares de la saga Total War. pool.titulo: Poll: Are You Still Happy To Pay For Online Multiplayer On Xbox Consoles?
pool.resumen:
I'm not sure paid multiplayer makes sense anymore.
Paying for access to online multiplayer has been the norm on Xbox consoles for decades now. It's something we've come to expect as part of playing online with friends and other folk around the world. The general understanding is, if you don't have Xbox Live, you're not playing online.
Eight years ago, I bought a gaming laptop to play Battlefield V on the go, and ever since paying for access to online multiplayer hasn't made much sense to me. It's just not something you do on PC. Sure, games like World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy XIV require additional subscriptions in order to play, but the majority of online games, like BFV, only require you to upfront the retail cost and crack on.
