pool.titulo: GTA 6 Owes Everything to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
pool.resumen: The one-two punch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Grand Theft Auto 6 made November a special month.
pool.contenido: There’s a lot that a Metacritic score can’t tell you. Look up the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the review aggregate site and you’ll find that it has a 99 . Impressive! What that number doesn’t capture, though, is how significant the reaction to Ocarina of Time felt in 1998. The critical awe was nothing short of unprecedented at that point in video game history — I remember some publications even going as far as to award it an 11/10. The atmosphere around what was being hailed as a revolutionary game made you feel like you were experiencing history. Looking back at that moment from 2026, it’s astounding that Ocarina of Time ’s legacy actually lived up to that hype long-term.

pool.titulo: Three Years After His Death, EA Is Using AI To Bring Back A Famed Commentator In FC 27
pool.resumen:
EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.
Motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005. According to the BBC , EA approached Motson's wife and son for permission to regenerate his voice and use his likeness for this year's entry in the series. Both agreed to the idea, but neither party has disclosed how much EA has paid for the use. Fred Motson, John's son, stated that he believed his father would've approved of this use of AI.
"My dad was the least technological person in the world," Fred stated. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk. So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically, but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects."

pool.titulo: Diablo 4’s Most Nostalgic Season Is Becoming (Mostly) Permanent
pool.resumen:
Diablo 4 is gearing up for the arrival of Season 16, but it won't be leaving its popular previous season behind entirely.
As detailed by Blizzard in a breakdown of the upcoming Season of Tyrael's Gambit, much of the previous season, Hell's Legacy, will become a permanent part of Diablo 4 going forward. Season 15 served as celebration of the franchise's history, and added a smorgasbord of items and callbacks to previous Diablo titles, including a storyline revolving around Deckard Cain and the return of enemies and boss encounters from Diablo 2.
Most of that is carrying forward, Blizzard said. Due to "overwhelming requests" from the game's community, Blizzard outlined what all from Hell's Legacy will survive.
Hell's Legacy's capstone dungeons will be added, as will the ability to summon a World Boss version of Diablo and take on the cow god Moopisto. The Prime Evil Council is also becoming permanent, and will work the same way the game's other Lair bosses do, with players needing a specific item to open their reward chest after successfully defeating the encounter.

pool.titulo: As the US Treasury suffers a cybersecurity breach, its chief tech guy is vibecoding a Civilization clone
pool.resumen: The DOGE alum Treasury CIO says his passion project is "so cool."
pool.contenido:
This week, amidst ongoing service disruptions, the US Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed that it is "investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems." The bureau, which collects and analyzes transaction data to combat financial crimes, says it has taken some of its e-filing systems offline "as a proactive measure."
FinCEN hasn't provided an estimate of when the investigation and system disruptions will be resolved, leaving the ability of financial institutions to report suspicious activity and interface with law enforcement indefinitely hampered. Meanwhile, as FinCEN is putting out fires, US Treasury chief information officer Sam Corcos has been busying himself with a different kind of work: He's been vibecoding a Civilization clone.
Corcos' LLM-powered game project was noticed by Bulwark economics editor Catherine Rampell: "The Treasury CIO appears to have spent the past three days vibecoding a Civilization game clone instead of working on this major Treasury database cyber breach," she wrote in a post on X . "As I type this, his Claude code is literally adding theme music."
A DOGE appointee who previously raised cybersecurity concerns at the IRS with an API "hackathon" and sought to cancel engineering efforts intended to modernize its systems, Corcos is hosting his little LLM project on Github. It's called Legatum, and he describes it as "historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization."
As Corcos writes in its readme, Legatum is "largely" built with the use of AI coding agents, and all of its art is AI-generated. While FinCEN addresses its cybersecurity breach, Corcos and his Claude agents have been steadily pushing updates: At time of writing, the latest commit —added just six minutes ago—tweaked some of its AI art.
Among the other half-dozen or so commits in the last three hours are adjustments to map generation, music updates, and—let's see— attempts at stemming "a wave of political issues and README vandalism" left by Github users.
That automated moderation evidently still needs some optimizing, judging from the repo's Issue #220 , which reads: "Lead developer is a giant asshole." Another issue notes that "late game American civilization feels broken," because "when you get the Large Language Model tech unlocked, it pretty much destroys any chance of a cultural victory because all your artists are gone, and all your government buildings become totally useless."
FinCEN isn't the only US government organization suffering cybersecurity issues this week. Yesterday, The New York Times reported that the CIA, the Office of the Director of National Security, and the Department of Defense's National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency had been impacted by a vulnerability in an open source intelligence system, which exposed unclassified information.
On X, Corcos has addressed the questionable optics of overseeing a vibecoded Civ knockoff while his department's facing a cybersecurity intrusion: "Just a heads up, the computers are doing it on their own," Corcos said in a reply to a user who compared the incident to Nero fiddling while Rome burned. "Mostly Opus 5.5 orchestrating a bunch of iterative loops."
In another reply to a more sympathetic user, Corcos was more enthusiastic: "These tools are getting so good it's blowing my mind. A brief voice note on my phone can kick off an amount of work that would have taken dozens of people weeks to deliver," he said. "So cool."

Sony has confirmed the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for December, which will be available to download from Tuesday, December 1 to Monday January 4.
In a PlayStation Blog post , Sony said Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, and Amnesia: The Bunker are December’s three titles. Will you be able to tear yourself away from GTA 6 to give either of these games a shot? Or perhaps you're after a palate cleanser after pumping 100 hours into Rockstar's epic?
IGN's Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4 review returned an 8/10. We said: "Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4 proves yet again the series’ over-the-top skateboarding formula is totally timeless, even if some of the changes to THPS4 miss the mark and the soundtrack has been fumbled."
Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, meanwhile, got a 7.5 back in 2017 . "Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 is an ambitious , if rough-edged experience, with deceptively deep RPG and brawling elements," we said at the time.
And our Amnesia: The Bunker review returned an 8. We said: "Amnesia: The Bunker is a smaller, more self-contained episode in the groundbreaking horror franchise that shows Frictional still has some chilling new tricks up their sleeves."

pool.titulo: Grab Star Wars: Zero Company for As Little as £32 in Amazon’s Black Friday Sale — Record-Low Prices on All Platforms
pool.resumen: Star Wars Zero Company has hit its lowest-ever price at Amazon UK, with up to 30% off PS5, Xbox, and PC editions in the Black Friday sale
pool.contenido:
Amazon UK has slashed the cost of Star Wars Zero Company for Black Friday , with all three versions of the tactical Star Wars adventure now selling for under £35, less than three months after its launch.
At the time of writing, you can grab the physical disc PS5 and Xbox Series X editions of Star Wars Zero Company for just £34.99 each at Amazon, down by £15 from their usual £49.99 RRPs; but the game on PC is now only £31.99 — the biggest deal of all, though this is the version that needs to be played via the EA App.
We Loved Star Wars Zero Company, And It's Getting A Big Discount For Black Friday Whichever platform you go for, those up to 30% discounts are the lowest prices Zero Company’s seen on the storefront — previously only dropping to as low as £39.99 before this month (confirmed with our own price-tracking tools).
Is Star Wars Zero Company Worth Buying? Developed by Bit Reactor alongside Respawn Entertainment, Zero Company takes place during the Clone Wars, putting you in command of a squad led by former Republic officer Hawks.
Rather than the usual purely lightsaber-heavy Star Wars action, it's a single-player, turn-based strategy game, featuring customisable operatives, tactical combat, and plenty of different abilities to experiment with.
In fact, IGN awarded Star Wars Zero Company a 9/10 and Editors' Choice in our August review of the game , praising its cinematic presentation, compelling characters, and refreshingly different take on XCOM-style combat.
Our colleague reviewer, Dan Stapleton, also spent approximately 35 hours finishing the campaign on Normal difficulty, so there's a considerable amount to get stuck into for what you’re spending.
What's more, Alinea Analytics estimated in September that the game had already sold around one million copies , although EA hasn't confirmed official figures. Still, that’s plenty of other players who’ve seemed to have agreed that this one’s worth buying at full price, so that’s even better value for you now you can get yours at up to £18 less.

pool.titulo: One of GTA 6's Best Features Was Actually Planned for GTA: Vice City, Reveals Ex-Rockstar Dev
pool.resumen: GTA 6's headphones mechanic was originally planned to be included in the original GTA: Vice City, according to a former Rockstar Games employee.
pool.contenido:
GTA 6's headphones mechanic was originally planned to be included in the original GTA: Vice City, according to a former Rockstar Games employee.
Ex-Rockstar Games dev Obbe Vermeji revealed that the headphones feature was cut from GTA: Vice City due to a technical reason, and they had even created an icon for it. It's unclear what the technical reason was, but Vice City's version likely would've come in the form of a Walkman or cassette player, given it was set in the 80s. GTA 6's version, however, comes with a smartphone and a pair of AirPods.
The feature is pretty incredible, because you can listen to music and podcasts wherever you go. You no longer have to sit in the car to finish a song; you can just get out, put your headphones in, and turn on the radio station you were just listening to. And when combined with combat encounters, it can have some thrilling results. Last night, In the Air Tonight came on as I approached a gang hideout, creating an incredibly cinematic moment for me.
This is the best game ever made dude https://t.co/AFR2jmo0fF
— Cade Onder (@Cade_Onder) November 25, 2026
It doesn't always have to lead to some epic moment, though. It's great for working out in-game, learning about the world and lore of GTA via podcasts and talk shows, and much more. A lot of effort has been packed into creating GTA 6's in-game media, and the headphones allow you to make full use of it. The only downside is that you can't make any kind of custom playlists. Presumably, this is because Rockstar wants players to organically discover music from the radio stations instead of curating the songs they already know and love.
The option would be nice, but personally, there are so many great songs I may have never heard if GTA's radio stations didn't expose me to them. Maybe a future update or the inevitable online mode will include a playlist option, but it could be a while before we see such a thing.

pool.titulo: This GTA 6 Radio Station Represents Its Florida-Inspired Setting Perfectly
pool.resumen: Southern hip-hop deserves its respect in rap history and GTA 6 celebrates it with its own radio station full of bangers from Outkast, T.I., Trick Daddy, Gucci Mane, and so many more.
pool.contenido:
Radio stations have always been a staple of Grand Theft Auto, filled with licensed (and some original) songs alongside crazy-ass talk shows. GTA 6 is unprecedented in this field, with its massive tracklist and over-the-top on-air personalities. But we all have the music genres we gravitate towards when picking out a station, and the one I'm rarely ever changing is Dirty South Classics – basically a playlist of the Southern hip-hop bangers I grew up listening to. It's also a thematic fit for GTA 6's setting of Leonida, an obvious parallel to the state of Florida.
While you traditionally wouldn't consider South Florida or the city of Miami part of the American South, the rest of Florida is largely culturally aligned with the region's states like Georgia, Mississippi, and parts of Texas (namely Houston). These are key distinctions to make in the context of music, especially what we consider Southern hip-hop – colloquially known as 'dirty south' hip-hop, hence the station name. Deep bass, rattling hi-hats, catchy melodies with instrumentals that either align with aggressive trap beats or the more soulful funk; characteristics of the genre that you hear throughout Dirty South Classics.
Because of its importance as a subgenre, and as a prominent cultural touchstone of the region that GTA 6 is trying to portray, it got its own dedicated station separate from VCRR, which is for more contemporary rap hits. So, admittedly, Dirty South Classics laser-targets oldheads who scrapped in the schoolyard in the early/mid 2000s – damn, I guess I really am unc now, huh. Hell, the station is hosted by Trick Daddy and Trina, two major figures in the Southern rap game from Miami (with interstitials from Gucci Mane himself). Just in the first few hours of my playthrough of GTA 6, I kept thinking to myself, 'They put this song in the game?!' And they all took me back to a very specific time and place as I rapped along off the top of the brain like I was a youngin' all over again.
I'm glad GTA 6 went with Outkast's "Player's Ball" instead of the Atlanta-based duo's more well-known hits. It has the quintessential sound of a classic Southern hip-hop track with a bold bassline and funky instrumentals rounded out with Andre 3000's falsetto hook. This particular style can be heard throughout their debut album "Southernplayalisticadillacmuzik" (1994) – although Outkast's sound changed in interesting ways afterward and exploded in popularity, it's still my favorite record of theirs.
Knuck If You Buck's first four notes activate any 30-something-year-old who had to square up and run the fade at school in a moment's notice. On the other end of the genre spectrum, I can’t believe I'm hearing Dem Franchize Boyz' "White Tee" in a game in the year 2026. It was their first song to break containment in 2004 and it's an ode to, well, the universality of the plain white t-shirt – affordable, easy to match in any outfit, and helpful in keeping a low profile, as covered in the song's lyrics. This especially resonated in the era of tall tees in my neighborhood, but I still don't understand the hostility toward throwbacks.
Maybe I shouldn't have been listening to them when I was a kid, but Three 6 Mafia's "Side 2 Side" was my favorite song from the Memphis-based trio. That dark, melancholic cello melody that runs throughout the track is undeniably catchy and Juicy J's flow on the last verse goes so hard. I'm a little surprised GTA 6 didn't go with the more popular remix featuring Bow Wow, but I am glad because the original version here is damn near perfect.
Lastly, I have to shout out "Knuck If You Buck" by Crime Mob and Lil Scrappy , the universal fight or flight mode anthem. Its dark, aggressive sound and trunk-knocking bass makes you feel invincible, and those first four notes activate any 30-something-year-old who had to square up and run the fade at school in a moment's notice.
I'm scratching the surface of the Dirty South Classics radio station, only four of the 39 songs which include hits from Big Tymers, T.I., Juvenile, Mike Jones (who? Mike Jones!) and so many more – that's not counting club bangers from Gucci Mane, Lil' Jon, Petey Pablo, among others. And it's just one of the 20 music stations featured in GTA 6 that include traditional Latin music, foreign covers of big hits, deep country, a roster of top-40 pop hits, and more. So, it's pretty nice that the biggest game in the world can also be a celebration of music, especially for a culture attached to its own setting.

pool.titulo: GTA 6: Breaking Down The Cleanest Bank Robbery We've Seen So Far
pool.resumen: One GTA 6 player has robbed $160,000 in just one minute in the cleanest bank robbery we’ve seen yet. Here's how they did it.
pool.contenido:
Warning: This article talks about gameplay mechanics from chapter four of GTA 6, but contains no story spoilers.
GTA 6 is a game all about making money. One of the quickest and most profitable ways of doing that is by robbing one of Vice City’s biggest banks. It’s also one of the riskiest, though; we’ve a legion of law enforcement destined to descend upon you once that alarm is triggered. That doesn’t mean a clean escape isn’t possible, though, and that’s just what one streamer has showcased, in perhaps the most impressive manner we’ve seen so far.
Video game streamer Sway set about his mission to the downtown Lombank for all its worth via a popular method – tailing a security van. These are the green and white vans you sometimes see driving around the map, which, if you follow for long enough, will lead you to a bank where the vault will be left wide open for you to enter. You can also make the locations of these trucks visible by paying Yasmani a hefty $10,000 tip for the info.
It’s worth noting that this option isn’t available until chapter four, with banks not being able to be successfully robbed at all until partway through GTA 6’s third chapter, once you gain the ability to cash in on marked bills. Otherwise, you’ll end up as Lucia can in the prologue, with a whole load of coloured dye all over you.
Anyway, back to Sway’s attempted heist, and just because the security guard has opened the vault doesn’t mean you can simply walk in and out of the building carrying a load of cash. There are numerous options you can take, including blasting your way in and getting in and out as quickly and violently as possible, or entering through the back rooms to sneak past everyone. The latter is the way that Sway mostly went with.
First, he shot out a security camera in the rear alley with a silenced pistol, before cracking open a garage door and quickly knocking out a guard with a quick pistol whip. Another couple of security members fell unconscious thanks to the blunt end of a gun as he made his way swiftly into the vault. Just noting the excellent choice of “old person” mask from Jason here, too.
Cleanest Bank Robbery you'll see in GTA 6.
$150k in 1 minute.
simple and clean. https://t.co/Y8GqDuydvd
— sway (@swaywtw) November 25, 2026
Next come the stacks of marked bills, which are hurriedly bundled into stash bags by Lucia. This action triggers the bank’s alarm systems, and always will, as far as I know. The cloud-based security camera system can’t be overrun and will always alert the cops once a couple of bundles of notes hit the bottom of your bag. With $122,000 already secured, he smartly swaps to controlling Jason, who can fill up his own bag to maximise the profits. With the grand total now sitting at $160,000, the hard part begins. At least, in theory, it should be difficult.
This clearly isn’t Sway’s first run, though, as he doesn’t panic at all. He runs back to where he entered from, kneecapping an onrushing guard with a single bullet before reopening the garage door to exit the bank and remove the couple’s masks, in turn removing the appearance marker from the top right. Cleverly, Lucia’s personal vehicle — a sleek sports car, yet another sign this isn’t his first heist if he can afford to register that — is sitting just feet away. He changes into a fresh pair of clothes, holsters his weapon, and just like that, becomes completely incognito. Little do the cops who have just rolled up know that the people walking past them are exactly who they’re at the bank for, and he simply walks across the road and out of the red circle on the minimap towards freedom.
It’s an incredibly quick, clean in-and-out operation, and the sort of robbery that feels extra satisfying to pull off in GTA 6. It’s the kind of hidden-in-plain-sight thrill that you’d expect from the likes of the Hitman series, but pulled off in a dynamic open world that loves to throw surprises your way. There’s no “correct” method, either. It can be just as fun to barrel through the main doors of a Fleeca and set a series of sticky bomb charges to gain access to the cash behind locked doors and inside safes. The huge-scale chases that can develop from botched escapes deliver a thrill, too, with chaos often reigning supreme.

27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD QD-OLED Gaming Monitor Most people would agree that OLED monitors are as good as it gets for gaming. They're also really expensive. Well, Alienware is bucking the trend with one of its latest 2026 OLED releases. The 27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD 240Hz QD-OLED gaming monitor is listed at an already reasonable retail price of $349.99, but for Black Friday it's down to just $279.99 with free shipping. This is a 27" 2560x1440 (QHD) monitor that incorporates a Samsung quantum dot OLED ( QD OLED ) panel, which is brighter and has a wider color gamut than the more commonly found W-OLED panel.
39" Alienware AW3926QW 5K RGB Tandem Stripe OLED Monitor Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology."It launched with a retail price of $1,099.99 but for Black Friday you can get it for $100 less . The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive inclusion is the LG RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.
The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.
32" Alienware AW3225QF 4K 240Hz QD-OLED Gaming Monitor Alienware's most popular 4K OLED gaming monitor is also down to its lowest price ever. If you're looking for the best 4K gaming monitor , this should definitely be on your short list. The Alienware AW3225QF is HDR True Black 400 certified with up to 1,000 nits of peak brightness. It also boasts a factory calibrated 99.3% DCI-P3 color range, 1700R curve, and G-Sync certification .
32" Alienware AW3226Q 4K RGB Tandem Stripe OLED Monitor The 32" Alienware AW3226Q gaming monitor is another recent release that's aimed toward the more budget-conscious crowd. pool.titulo: The Witcher 3 and Assassin's Creed 'Reset Player Expectations' for Open-World Action RPGs, So the Fable Reboot Devs Had to Look Beyond the Original Trilogy for Inspiration
pool.resumen: Why has the Fable reboot taken so long to develop? There are a number of reasons, but part of it is that expectations around open-world action RPGs were reset by various competing games over the past decade.
pool.contenido:
Why has the Fable reboot taken so long to develop? There are a number of reasons, but part of it is that expectations around open-world action RPGs were reset by various competing games over the past decade.
Work on Fable reportedly started in 2016, and only now, 10 years later, is it near release. It’s suffered a tumultuous development but, unlike some other costly Microsoft gaming projects, it has avoided closure amid sweeping layoffs and restructuring at Xbox.
In a new interview with GamesIndustry.biz , Playground Games co-founder and Fable general manager Ralph Fulton touched on the trials and tribulations Fable has endured over the years. Playground set up a new team to make Fable in addition to its hugely popular racing game franchise, Forza Horizon, and set out to make a game in a genre it had no prior experience with. And Fable is a big role-playing game, with all the bells and whistles you'd expect. So, Fable isn’t technically a debut game from Playground, but it sort of is.
In terms of what’s changed, Fulton said that technology had “advanced” during development, pointing to a reset of player expectations with the release of CD Projekt’s fantasy RPG masterpiece The Witcher 3 and then Assassin’s Creed’s move towards the RPG genre.
This, Fulton explained, meant that Playground had to look beyond the original Fable trilogy for inspiration to ensure it created a reboot that would meet modern open-world standards.
“In 2015, The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard,” Fulton explained. “And after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG.
“All of these games continue to reset player expectations, which means I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects.”
Despite this, the scope of Fable actually decreased over time, with the project starting with “an enormous potential scope.” In August, Playground confirmed that Fable’s main quest will take around 20 hours to beat , with an additional 15-20 hours of side and open-world exploration content available. Howlongtobeat has the original 2004 Fable 's main quest clocking in at about 12-and-a-half hours. Fable 2 isn't much longer at 13 hours , and Fable 3 inches just further past that at 13-and-a-half hours . So, the Fable reboot is shaping up to be the longest in the series.
Fable is set for launch on February 23, 2027, across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S.

pool.titulo: Deceased BBC football commentator resurrected with AI for EA Sports FC: The family says it's a 'touching tribute' but some fans call it 'gross' and 'bleak'
pool.resumen: Legendary football pundit John Motson will return to the series, in AI form, in today's EA FC 27 title update.
pool.contenido:
Legendary BBC football commentator John "Motty" Motson, who died in 2023 at age 77, is being added to EA Sports FC 27 through "a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself." The AI-powered recreation of Motson's distinctive voice has the blessing of his family, but some fans of the game are less than enthused.
Motson's history with EA's football series goes back more than 30 years, to FIFA Soccer 96 (which came out in 1995). His last game in that series was FIFA Soccer 2005, according to Mobygames , but he continued to work with EA Sports on the FIFA Manager series. The announcement of his posthumous return to the series says "almost 10 years of in-game recordings" were used in conjunction with "new AI tools" to put Motson's voice in EA FC 27.
"My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA Sports FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game," John's son Fred said. "His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole new set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary."
Fred Motson told the BBC that he believes his father "absolutely" would have wanted his voice to be the game after his death: "I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically—but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects." The BBC report also notes that EA paid the Motson family an undisclosed sum for the right to use John's voice.
Not everyone shares Fred Motson's enthusiasm. While plenty in the EA Sports FC subreddit are excited by the prospect, others refer to it with terms like "shameful," "disrespectful," "gross," and "bloody dark."
"What a bleak fucking world we live in," redditor forameus2 wrote. "You can't even escape in death."
"Honestly, it's kind of gross for me," jlo1989 added.
"If anyone from my family uses AI to resurrect me in some perverse way like this, I'll fucking haunt them," niallmul97 wrote.
Peter Caulfield of the Save Our Voices Now campaign against unauthorized voice cloning told the BBC he wouldn't care if Motson had signed a deal with EA allowing it to use his likeness after his death. "But in life or death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed," Caufield said, adding that family members shouldn't "automatically" have the right to grant permission for AI recreations either.
At least one other game studio has taken a very different approach to the subject: Earlier this year, Darkest Dungeon developer Red Hook Studios said it would never use AI to recreate the voice of beloved narrator Wayne June, who died in 2025, despite having explicit permission from June himself to do so: "I would never, ever erode his incredible and timeless performances by teaching a machine to sound like him," Red Hook co-founder Chris Bourassa said at the time. The Japan Actors Union also recently began a push to protect the rights of voice actors with regard to AI, including a proposed ban on using AI to copy a dead actor's voice unless consent had been obtained prior to their death.

pool.titulo: 'People Are Doing It Too Quickly Now' — The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Director Speaks Out on YA Franchise Reboots
pool.resumen: I got the chance to sit down with the director of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence, who opened up about the amount of remakes happening in Hollywood and how he would feel if The Hunger Games series ever got rebooted.
pool.contenido:
I got the chance to sit down with the director of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence, who opened up about the amount of remakes happening in Hollywood and how he would feel if The Hunger Games series ever got rebooted.
Francis Lawrence has directed all but one movie in The Hunger Games series. He’s been with the franchise for over a decade; the first film, directed by Gary Ross, released in 2012, after which Lawrence took up the mantle for all subsequent movies.
It’s one of several iconic movie franchises that defined the YA boom of the 2000s - mid-2010s. And unlike other series from this time period, it has neither languished nor suffered a reboot before its corpse is even cold.
HBO’s forthcoming Harry Potter series is perhaps the most egregious example of such a reboot. The last Harry Potter movie released in 2011, and its cast defined an entire generation of fans who grew up watching their adventures at Hogwarts. It seems almost insulting to reimagine the world that was so painstakingly built over the course of a decade — but that’s just my opinion.
I’m not alone in this line of thinking, though. When asked about his feelings on reboots, Lawrence agreed that they’re happening too soon, bringing up Warner Bros.’ thankfully canceled idea for an I Am Legend reboot in 2014, just seven years after the original film was released.
“I mean, I do feel like people are doing it sort of too quickly now,” he mused. “I agree with you on that. People started talking about that with I Am Legend. I don't remember how long ago, but it felt like 10 years had gone by or something, and somebody was thinking of remaking it already at Warner. I'm like, ‘Really? 10 years, that's it?’”
Given the imminent release of HBO’s Harry Potter series on Christmas day, I had to bring up the very real possibility that The Hunger Games sees a reboot in the next decade or so — an idea that Lawrence wasn’t sure would get Suzanne Collins’ blessing.
“I don't know how I would feel about it,” he admitted. “I also don't know if Suzanne has anything in place to sort of protect against that, but that'd be really, really interesting to figure out. But I think it's a tough one. I mean, if Suzanne backed it, I think some spinoffs, and obviously if she writes other books, things like that could be interesting, as long as she backs it and comes up with it and has the thematic reasonings and philosophies that she usually does, that would be cool. But I don't know how you go back and remake the original movies and it not be [Jennifer Lawrence]."
To his point, The Hunger Games franchise has managed to stay in the public consciousness, owing in part to its later release during the YA boom (the final film in the original series came out in 2015) and its two prequel movies that rocked theaters in the 2020s. The latest movie, Sunrise on the Reaping , received solid reviews from critics, earning an 8 out of 10 from IGN.
For more news on this newest entry in The Hunger Games series, check out my interview with star Joseph Zada , who told me all about how he managed to pull off Woody Harrelson's unmistakable accent, and whether or not the cast is Team Peeta or Team Gale .

pool.titulo: GTA 6 Doesn't Let You Replay Missions, and Rockstar Says There's a Good Reason for That
pool.resumen: GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar.
pool.contenido:
GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar.
When speaking with Kotaku , Rockstar Games senior design director Scott Butchard explained why the studio scrapped a mission replay menu in GTA 6. Both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 allowed players to freely replay missions, but that's not the case in GTA 6 . According to Butchard, they considered bringing the feature back, but cut it because it was "at odds" with the story.
“Mission replay was certainly something we looked at early on in development, and we do not currently support it,” said Butchard. “As the game came together it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected. Sitting outside of the game as it were and replaying missions really diminished the choices you had made.”
The lack of a mission replay option has been a point of contention for fans. GTA 6 has some of the best missions in the franchise, particularly the final mission of Chapter 1. Given that GTA 6 can take players anywhere from 50 - 100 hours to finish, most people probably won't start the entire game over just to re-experience their favorite mission. However, it's worth noting that Butchard says the game doesn't "currently support" this feature. Maybe it'll come in the form of an update later, but Rockstar hasn't confirmed that.
GTA 6's story and missions can deviate somewhat significantly based on your choices. Certain characters can be killed or spared, objectives can be completed in different ways, and the entire relationship between Jason and Lucia can vary based on your actions. You can get entirely different dialogue options and cutscenes based on these differences, which might be why a mission replay system isn't as straightforward as it was previous games.
However, Red Dead Redemption 2 also featured different choices that changed Arthur's character. It wasn't quite as nuanced as GTA 6's variations, though. Maybe Rockstar will figure out a way to do this, but it clearly fell low on the priority list, if it was on the list at all by the end of development. Even if Rockstar never adds it, modders will probably find a way to slot it in when the inevitable PC version releases.

pool.titulo: 'It Would Be Absolutely Incredible' — Hideki Kamiya Wants to Make a New Castlevania Game With Konami
pool.resumen: Hideki Kamiya, the mind behind Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and Okami, wants to make a new Castlevania game, saying his team at CLOVERS could make something “absolutely incredible.”
pool.contenido:
Hideki Kamiya, the mind behind Devil May Cry , Bayonetta , and Okami , wants to make a new Castlevania game, saying his team at CLOVERS could make something "absolutely incredible" alongside Konami.
Hideki Kamiya is back in the saddle at CLOVERS, his independent game studio made up of former CLOVER staff who are currently hard at work on the Okami sequel . He made the company’s independent status extremely clear in his latest YouTube video , reminding excited fans to stop asking him about Capcom-owned franchises (or even sequels to games like God Hand , since he had no part in its development).
Given CLOVERS’ status as an independent company that’s already working with a major developer in Capcom, Kamiya floated ideas for future collaborations with other big developers once the Okami sequel is out in the world. One of those ideas was a partnership with Konami for a Castlevania game, which he promised would be “incredible,” if it actually ends up happening.
“Since we’re independent and don’t have any outside funding, we want to stay on good terms — or rather, collaborate — with various companies and keep doing interesting things,” he explained. “Of course, I want to keep building a good relationship with Capcom, and naturally, I’d like to be on good terms with Nintendo, too.
“...Maybe I could make a new Getsufumaden with Konami. Oh, and Castlevania. If we made it, it would be absolutely incredible, so please, let us take the job. I am a bit busy right now, though,” he laughed.
A Castlevania game from a mind like Kamiya’s would definitely be something special. Would it be a 3D action game like Bayonetta, or more of a 2D side-scroller in the vein of Viewtiful Joe ? The possibilities are endless, and given that Konami is already on a mission to revitalize its classic IPs with new games, the possibility of a team-up with CLOVERS on a Castlevania title isn’t totally out of the question.
It's also worth noting that the Castlevania franchise enjoyed a new installment in Belmont's Curse late last month. Alongside its animated adaptations on Netflix, Konami's classic vampire-slaying game series is getting a second wind, and Kamiya would like to be part of that, though whether or not this actually happens remains to be seen.
Kamiya also brought up ideas for other potential games that CLOVERS might make in collaboration with big publishers in the future, though how serious he was about these is up to interpretation. He playfully mentioned making a Star Fox sequel with Koei Tecmo or a King’s Knight sequel with Square Enix, and even mentioned a Kinnikuman M.U.S.C.L.E.: Tag Team Match game with Bandai Namco. Of course, these are all just goofy ideas he likely said in jest, but it does seem like he’s eager to make more games with major companies once Okami is out the door.
The Okami sequel was first announced at the 2024 Game Awards. It’s only been two years since then, so it’s unlikely that we’ll hear anything else from CLOVERS about the game’s development process anytime soon. However, you can read our exclusive interview with Kamiya , done just after the sequel’s TGA announcement, or check out our chat with him from the Lucca Comics & Games Festival just last month.

pool.titulo: GTA 6 has weird purple streetlights because actual Florida screwed up its streetlights
pool.resumen: Rockstar recreated an embarrassing mishap in Florida infrastructure.
pool.contenido:
When you're exploring a world as realistic and well-observed as GTA 6's Leonida, it's rare for a piece of benign infrastructure to stick out. But on night one of my playthrough, I clocked some weird streetlights.
Why are some of them turquoise?
And hey, why are these purple?
A stylistic choice by Rockstar? Maybe, but it's awfully specific, and I had a feeling there was a deeper intention behind it. So I DMed my buddy Henry, an honest-to-god Floridian who was also playing GTA 6, and asked what's up. At first he thought strange streetlights in the Key Lento area of the map were special lights meant to not disorient turtles, but those are typically red, so probably not. And that doesn't explain the purple ones.
So Henry reached out to friends in south Florida, the region that Leonida's biggest cities are based on, and they cracked the case wide open.
"The purple [lights] are definitely real. We have a ton of them down here because whoever is in charge of that in the government bought a bunch of defective lights," the anonymous Floridian responded.
Yes, actual Florida cities are lit by these dubiously dim, yet undeniably cool purple lamps. According to ClickOrlando , residents first started reporting the purple streetlights in 2023. They put up hundreds of these things across the state before they started malfunctioning—it was such a kerfuffle that the government eventually released a statement saying their vendor really screwed the pooch.
Apparently the cause was a "spectral shift caused by phosphor displacement," which essentially means the LED lights were always blue, but the coating that was supposed to make appear yellow or white or whatever didn't work. The powers that be said the malfunctioning lights would be replaced, but judging by our own sources in the state, they haven't gotten them all.
So that's fun. If you already heard about this somewhere (other than your Floridian friend), it's probably because YouTuber AnyAustin also clocked these lights in his video published yesterday. Glad I'm not the only one who couldn't resist this rabbit hole.
I like how Rockstar didn't go overboard with these lights—just like the genuine article, they're in and around parts of Leonida, but not everywhere. I'm still not sure how to explain the turquoise ones, though. A lot of local news, Reddit, and YouTube skimming did not produce a clear answer, other than other cities in America that do have green streetlights sometimes. Perhaps Key Lento has lamps busted in a slightly different way, or it's just a calming shade of blue that Rockstar thought looked nice. It does, to be fair.

pool.titulo: Warhammer Survivors update buffs XP and weapons, nerfs those damn Beasts of Nurgle
pool.resumen: I hate those guys.
pool.contenido:
If you've played over a hundred hours of Vampire Survivors you've probably forgotten how slow its early progression feels. It certainly seemed that way based on the reaction to Warhammer Survivors from Vampire Survivors veterans, who complained about its grindiness compared to their beloved bullet heaven originator, despite the arc of both games being quite similar. Developers Auroch Digital made Warhammer Survivors in partnership with Vampire Survivors creator Poncle, so of course the two games have a lot in common.
Other complaints were more valid. The Beasts of Nurgle did have too many hit points, and their ability to regenerate only exacerbated that. The treasure chest-opening animation did take a bit too long. And some of the weapons were undertuned. Fortunately, those issues and more have been addressed in hotfix v2.18 . Here are the highlights:
Balance changes to weapons and enemies, improving weapon damage on select weapons, an aim-assist on the Boltgun and a reduction of max health points on various enemies (including that gargantuan Carnifex!). Added a health bar for enemy minibosses. With the introduction of a new grey Skull Gem, enemies will now always provide some amount of XP. Improved weapon projectile collision on various stages as well as continued improvements to prevent chests dropping at inaccessible locations. Playable champions now break Light Sources when they walk over them. Shortened the Treasure Chest animation, and it is now more common to encounter a rare chest if your luck has been poor. Reduced the volume of the self-destruct alert sound effect. The change to XP is an interesting one. It's a standard part of the genre's formula to have random XP drops—killing some enemies gives you nothing, while others drop XP gems and tempt you to rush into a mob to grab them. Making every enemy drop at least a low-value XP gem will speed up leveling a bit, but hopefully when you see green or red gems you'll still want to risk a mob of orks to yoink.
Auroch Digital recently revealed a roadmap of upcoming additions to Warhammer Survivors, with the first big update in December promising more characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions. January's updates will add more quality-of-life and balance improvements, as well as cross-save, with another update in the first quarter of 2027 bringing another round of characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions.
The final item on the roadmap is a tease that simply says, "ERROR… Details classified." It's probably not the addition of a whole extra universe to its current Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar settings, but I'd be stoked to see them add the other popular world of Warhammer. By which I mean Blood Bowl, of course.

pool.titulo: Capcom's quirky dinosaur-fighting hero shooter is shutting down in 2027
pool.resumen: Exoprimal was intriguing, but it never caught fire with players.
pool.contenido:
"Exoprimal is a throwback to weird, experimental early 2000s Capcom ," we wrote of the team-based hero shooter ahead of its launch back in 2023. While ostensibly about battling dinosaurs, "you first go through an interdimensional time portal controlled by a rogue AI, and then you compete in a Hunger Games-style contest against alternate universe versions of yourself for the AI's amusement. That's where the dinosaur killing comes in."
Despite that intriguing premise, the end result was not particularly memorable: Perfectly fine, and with some fantastic ideas, but "more like an early access phase than a finished game," we wrote in our 69% review . And it didn't catch on: A year later, Capcom announced the end of new updates for the game, although the game remained fully playable.
But now that's changing too. Capcom announced today that Exoprimal services will be terminated on September 29, 2027 , at which point the game will become unplayable. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years," Capcom wrote, "and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement."
The sale of seasonal "survival passes," which have been rotating through Exoprimal's four seasons since the end of updates in 2024, has been halted, while the game itself along with all DLC and "other products"—there's quite a lot of it —will be removed from sale on March 30, 2027. After that, the game will tick on—and Capcom hopes you will continue to enjoy it—until the end of the road in September.
It sucks to see games fail, especially when they have the potential to grow into something good, and it's even worse when they don't just tank but become completely unplayable because of their reliance on external servers that no longer exist. This is one of the primary drivers behind efforts like Stop Killing Games : Wherever possible, the end of a game's service should not signal the end of the game.
It's a principle I broadly support, but in the case of Exoprimal it's fair to say that not too many people will be impacted by the shutdown: SteamDB indicates that the peak concurrent player count over the past 24 hours was just 23. Exoprimal is also available on consoles so there are more players in total than just that, but how many more? I don't know, but I'd guess not too many.

pool.titulo: Trump admin didn't investigate Jensen Huang before pushing Nvidia to bring him back: 'What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what?'
pool.resumen: Nvidia is also not under investigation, according to US Attorney General Todd Blanche.
pool.contenido:
US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he'd given Nvidia "assurance" that ousted and now reinstated CEO Jensen Huang did not represent a national security threat despite an affair with a woman who was reportedly in contact with China's top spy agency.
Trump provided that assurance without any formal investigation into Huang's dealings.
On whether Huang had been investigated, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said during a press conference this week, "I don't want to talk about investigation. What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what? I don't understand the question."
Blanche also said that he did not know about any export control investigation related to Nvidia, even though potential violations of export control law are the central concern of the scandal.
"A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race," Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer said on Tuesday.
According to sources speaking to Reuters , Trump's assurance to the Nvidia board was based on investigations into Nvidia clients Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed International, the latter of which is the company associated with Alice Huang (no relation), the woman with whom Huang admitted to having an affair. (The CEO also reportedly had affairs with Nvidia employees.)
In his return address to Nvidia staff, Huang said (via Marisa Kabas ) that the company's board opted to bring him back of their own accord, not because of pressure from the Trump administration. That statement is contradicted by Trump himself, who told CNBC that he "convinced" the Nvidia board to bring Huang back.
Nvidia's share price shot up following Huang's reinstatement, but dropped again by several points on Wednesday, and remains about 21.5% lower than it was at the start of this year. Trump is an Nvidia investor, and Nvidia donated $25 million to Trump's White House ballroom project.
Huang is scheduled to testify before the US Senate next Thursday, December 3.

pool.titulo: GTA 6 vault: How to open them during big bank jobs
pool.resumen: You can make well over $100,000 in a single crime if you open the bank vault and safe deposit boxes.
pool.contenido:
Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a big score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist.
But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission , you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.
Here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you. Only then can you steal all that sweet cash.
HOW TO OPEN A BANK VAULT Complete jobs for Yasmani Your GTA 6 fence , Yasmani, will begin offering you tips once you start selling him stolen goods in Chapter 3: jewelry store heists targeting specific items and which ATM jobs have the most cash, for example. These are worth doing anyway as they get you the snap gun .
Complete every job Yasmani has and keep asking for more, and in Chapter 4 he'll offer you a tip for $10,000. Pay it, and he'll give you the locations of two security vans (armored cars) in Vice City. They'll show up on your map as pink icons.
Or, search Vice City for armored cars on your own There are multiple banks with vaults that armored cars visit. While driving around the areas near these banks and keeping your eyes peeled, you may spot an armored car without Yasmani's tip. It could take quite a while, though!
You can see which banks have vaults by looking under "Big Bank Jobs" in the "Robberies" category on your map. There are four big banks in Ocean Beach, two downtown, one in Tequesta, and one at Vice City International Airport.
Follow an armored car to a bank Follow the armored car until it parks outside a bank. Watch as one of the drivers gets out and walks into the bank. You can follow him to see where he goes, though bank layouts differ and he may take different routes. He may walk through the front doors, or he may go in a side entrance or a roll-up door in the back.
Once he's all the way inside—not just inside the front doors, but deep into the bank—he'll head to the vault and open it.
You can't open that vault yourself! Only the armored car driver can. That's the trick.
Find the vault Once the guard is in the back of the bank, begin the robbery. Search for the vault in the back. You may need to use explosives to open the door the guard went through, or you can look for a door you can open with the snap gun. You'll find the vault door open with the armored car driver nearby. Subdue him and grab all the cash off the cart inside the vault.
BONUS LOOT Safe deposit boxes There are several safe deposit boxes in the vault you can open for extra loot. Use your focus ability to highlight which boxes you can loot, and shoot them to open them up. You can also blow open all the boxes at once using a grenade or sticky bomb. Grab the loot from each.
The cash drawers and safe If you really want to clean the place out, there's still all the cash drawers in the front of the bank and a small safe, or multiple safes, somewhere else, usually in an office in the back. You can open these standard safes with safe codes .
The armored car The armored car parked outside has loot in it, too. The thing is, it may despawn while you're inside the bank. If you want to loot it, place a sticky explosive on the rear door, which won't let the truck despawn. (Be stealthy: there's another guard still watching the truck). When you leave the bank after the robbery, detonate the bomb and grab the loot.
VAULT JOB TIPS Enter the bank through the back if possible The best way to enter a bank is through a back door, if the building has one, (using the snap gun to avoid alarms) or a roll-up door. If the guard you're following goes in the back, he may leave the doors unlocked behind him, and you may not even have to unlock any doors at all to reach the vault. Just be prepared to run into multiple security guards and employees you'll need to subdue.
Play as a couple You will want both Jason and Lucia along for any bank vault jobs you pull. There is so much cash and valuables to grab you'll easily fill up four bags, which requires two people to carry. (You can hand loot bags to your partner by interacting with them and choosing the "Hand over bag" prompt). You'll also want one character to work as crowd control while you're looting the bank.
Bring silenced weapons A silenced gun is a good idea: you want to delay setting off alarms for as long as possible, and if bank employees or citizens hear gunshots they may panic and trigger the alarm, or flee from the bank and call the cops.
Look for cloud-based security cameras In a lot of robberies you can find the security footage and destroy it while the robbery is in progress. Big banks have cloud-based cameras which won't allow you to destroy the footage. Keep a lookout (using focus) for cameras and shoot them out (with silenced pistols) as quickly as you can.
Plan an escape route If an alarm goes off during a vault robbery, you'll get an instant four-star wanted level, which means SWAT trucks, roadblocks, and helicopters. Park your car in a good spot outside so you can jump into it easily, and have some idea of where you want to drive to during your escape.

pool.titulo: Sunrise on the Reaping Director Reveals That Every Hunger Games Movie Has Initially Been Rated R
pool.resumen: Longtime director of The Hunger Games franchise Francis Lawrence has revealed that all five films he has directed in the series were initially rated R and opened up about the process of making them PG-13.
pool.contenido:
Longtime director of The Hunger Games franchise Francis Lawrence has revealed that all five films he directed in the series were initially rated R, prompting clever workarounds when editing them.
On paper, The Hunger Games franchise is tonally very interesting. Although it's a young adult novel series, targeting teenagers, it's about children being forced to fight to the death in a dystopian society. The books don't hold back on the violence, and the films have always had to walk a fine line so they can reach the widest audience possible. The process of making the movies PG-13 is complicated and often inconsistent.
When speaking with Kevin McCarthy , director Francis Lawrence noted that all five of the Hunger Games films he has worked on were initially rated R. The director noted that across his whole career, he has run into an issue of making a movie with a PG-13 rating in mind, but the MPA (Motion Picture Association) reserves the right to give it an R if it's too "intense," even if there's no excessive blood, gore, language, or nudity. It happened with Constantine, it was a concern with I Am Legend, and it has happened regularly with The Hunger Games series.
In one of the Mockingjay films, Lawrence had to cut a scene of a little girl crying and screaming over the body of her dead mother. There wasn't any blood, but the performance was so visceral that it pushed the film closer to an R-rating.
He revealed that the process is somewhat subjective, as the people who rate the movies change, their tastes change, and he was even able to identify specific changes on particular movies.
In regards to Sunrise on the Reaping, he believes that the MPA has become more "conservative" with their judgment of a film, prompting them to tweak the project and show it to the organization four or five times. He also said that sometimes he makes the content more intense on purpose when presenting it to the MPA, so when they edit it, they can show the "intended" version, and it looks more tame by comparison. One example of this is amplifying sound effects to make it sound gnarlier, and then reigning it in on subsequent edits.
Lawrence went on to note that he is surprised by how much these movies can get away with in a PG-13 context, but believes there's a thematic relevance that the MPA accepts.
"It does help that there's been so many of these now that there's [a] precedent," he said. "There's also real thematic relevance to these stories, and I think that also really helps, that in the end they're anti-violence stories. They're about the consequences of violence, the consequences of war; they're really about themes that are educating people. I do think the MPA takes that into consideration when they look at sequences that are intense. They have different emotional values, and it's not really splattercore, in a way.
"But I definitely do intensify beyond a limit of where I think it will be accepted as PG-13 purposely, because I know we are going to have to pull back on certain things."
He explained that certain deaths were more brutal and gratuitous in initial cuts of the film, but ultimately had to be adjusted for a PG-13 rating.
"One thing I really wanted to keep was we had a very specific neck wound on Maysilee in her death. Basically the one that kills her is right here," said Lawrence while pointing at the center of his neck. "And he's covering it and when his hand comes off, you can see blood starting to drip out of it, and you can see the hole, and it's why she can't speak. And they made us get rid of that, and that's what killed me."
The Hunger Games films are far from the only big mainstream action movies that have to get creative with how they depict violence. Crew members on The Dark Knight were confident the film would be rated R, despite Christopher Nolan and the studio working to avoid that. They were able to get around a harder rating thanks to the fact the film does most of the gorier acts of violence off-screen or even playing it off as a joke.
"It’s kind of shocking that The Dark Knight ended up being PG-13," said the film's cinematographer Wally Pfister in a 2018 interview . "All of Chris’s movies would be PG-13 to open it up to a wider audience. Somehow, he always had some magic with the MPA.
"Lo and behold, he has the pencil and I’m like, 'You are not getting the PG-13 with that. There’s no way this is going in. He’s driving this pencil through a guy’s head!' And I was wrong. Chris was always right, whether you liked it or not. You’d be like, 'F*** you, you were right again.' With this pencil trick, I thought, ‘If it has the right amount of levity, we’ll sell this and it won’t come off as being violent but it’ll come off as being a magic trick and it’ll come off as being a punchline.’ And it was!"
Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now.

In return, Sauron promises to free the creature and give it Khazad-dûm to rule. Co-showrunner Patrick McKay told IGN that Tolkien’s text describing the Balrog influenced how they interpreted the fire beast.
“One of the things that's cool in the books is if you really look into the lore that Tolkien built for his entire life, the Balrogs are intelligent super-beings,” McKay explained. “They aren't just monsters. They're cunning and they are battlefield commanders in the First Age. It opened up the possibility that we could show you a different side of him. Maybe one you're not expecting, but one that actually is true to the books and the conception.”
McKay and Episode 7 director Stefan Schwartz described the scene in the Misty Mountains as a dramatic “negotiation” between the Balrog and Sauron. “The scene goes from [Balrog’s] total disdain to actually being won over by Sauron to actually helping him in his quest to create this ring,” Schwartz pointed out.
'They aren't just monsters. They're cunning and they are battlefield commanders in the First Age.' McKay said casting director Theo Park came up with the idea of asking Simon Pegg to voice the Balrog opposite Charlie Vickers’ Sauron. “Simon Pegg is often known as a comedic actor because of the earliest films he did with Edgar Wright, but he can kind of do anything,” McKay said. “This was an opportunity to do something he hadn't done before, and he took to it like a duck to water.”
Schwartz confirmed that Pegg was on set, performing live into a microphone to Vickers, who was looking at a light box which represented the Balrog’s placement in the frame. “They could rehearse it and run the lines and then actually play it, and then we could talk about the nuance of how he is brought over to Sauron's way of thinking,” he said.
An ally of Sauron’s by the end of Season 3, the Balrog’s rule over King Thrain (Eddie Marsan) and the dwarves will play out in Season 4 (and 5 if it gets a greenlight).
The Fell Beasts: Sauron’s Dark Ride In the opening minutes of Episode 4, "Gundabad," Sauron is introduced to his future steed — an extremely ornery beast that is resistant to the bridle. In Tolkien’s letters, the author described them as winged, stinking creatures with no feathers, just bare skin. The author also referred to them as fell beasts, as well as Nazgûl-birds, which makes sense because in the book version of The Return of the King, fell beasts become the replacement steeds for the Ringwraiths.
However in The Rings of Power, Sauron expounds on their origins more specifically, telling the orcs, “They were once eagles, you know. Until Morgoth blessed them with his touch. Taught them to crave his lash, to survive on only the foulest of meats.” Because of that, Sauron knows the way to tame one is through feeding it living flesh, which he does by feeding it random orcs. The steady meals allow Sauron to bridle the beast, which he first uses to chase Galadriel to Mount Gundabad and then the forests of Greenwood. By the end of the season, Sauron has taught Nazgnagôl Theo ( Tyroe Muhafidin ), and likely the others, how to ride a fell beast. He uses it to dive-bomb the Númenórean army and freak out their soldiers on the eve of battle. Look for them to return when the real war between Sauron and Middle-earth begins in a future season.
The Great Eagle: Saving Our Heroes (Again) In the last minutes of "Gundabad," before Galadriel, Arondir, Celeborn and Marnûkh are trapped by Sauron and Nazgnagôl Theo on a ledge in Mount Gundabad, Galadriel releases a flaming arrow into the sky like a rescue flare. It spurs a snow-covered Giant Eagle in the mountain to awaken and fly into action. Galadriel instantly recognizes it is Landroval, Prince of Eagles. He gets hit by an orc arrow but survives to save Galadriel and Celeborn from falling to their deaths.
Landroval is a heroic figure across Tolkien’s ages. In The Hobbit, the eagle will save Thorin and company from the burning trees. And at the end of The Return of the King, Landroval is one of the three Great Eagles who rescue Frodo Baggins and Samwise Gamgee from Mordor after they destroy the One Ring.
The Oliphaunts: The Gandalf Connection The elephant-like creatures found south of Mordor are called oliphaunts in Tolkien’s text, and are formally introduced in The Rings of Power in Episode 3, "The Secret Fire.” Gandalf comes upon one in battle armor under the Dark Magic control of Pallando (Ciarán Hinds). pool.titulo: GTA 6 Animation Director Reveals Rockstar Made 3 Animations for Each Item Interaction
pool.resumen: Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.
pool.contenido:
Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.
If you’ve been playing GTA 6 at all, you’ve probably picked up on the fact that characters can now hold an item in each hand. This has made for some especially funny clips on social media, where users have wasted no time making Jason recreate the ‘six-seven’ meme while holding various objects.
This is a big change from previous Rockstar games; in titles like GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 , players could only carry one thing at a time, though you could dual wield certain guns in GTA: San Andreas. (You could also hold longarms at your side while shooting a pistol in RDR 2 and Max Payne 3 .) Now, you can hold a sandwich in one hand and a drink in the other — or a bag and a gun, if you’re sticking up a pawn shop, for instance. This isn’t just an aesthetic feature, either, as it serves the important function of letting players take care of two tasks at once, making robberies or transporting items a bit smoother.
Players have praised GTA 6 for its jaw-dropping attention to detail, and this particular tidbit wasn’t lost on them. A thread on Bluesky discussing the feature caught the attention of Mike Jones, the director of gameplay on Rockstar’s latest title, who revealed the extent of the studio’s efforts in making sure every single item interaction had a single-handed, two-handed, and hands-free animations.
“FYI, we made three versions for all item interactions; one if both hands are free, one if just your right hand is free and again for the left,” he wrote . “It was a massive pain, but once you knew every interaction could ‘cope,’ it made the game logic much easier. That was then sometimes replicated for crouch, too…”
That being said, the devs at Rockstar aren’t superheroes, and they had to cut corners somewhere during development. Jones admitted this fact in response to another comment in this thread, where a user wrote, “Honestly, the level of polish is so absurd that when I see how cheated the ‘putting gas in the car’ sequence is, I'm like, relieved. ‘Oh, okay, they're human, they bleed.’ You all did SO well.”
“Thanks, everyone would really appreciate your comments! And yes, shortcuts were definitely made, too,” Jones replied.
GTA 6 is a game like no other. Its world is so massive and detailed that some players are avoiding progressing the story in favor of chilling out in Key Lento and diving for treasure, fishing with Cal, and playing billiards at the Rusty Anchor. And we can’t blame them; there’s tons of stuff to do, even in Chapter 1.

If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . pool.titulo: All of the Harry Potter Interactive Illustrated Editions Are on Sale for Black Friday
pool.contenido:
There are a lot of different versions of the Harry Potter books . There's the original hardcovers, paperbacks with stencilled edges, and even a full-on Hogwarts trunk filled with the books you can buy. If you're looking for a gift to buy the Potter fan in your life in 2026, it can be a little overwhelming to decide exactly what set of books is worth purchasing for their collection. If you're buying for someone who has already read the entire series multiple times over, however, I'd suggest going with the illustrated editions that Amazon currently has in its buy 2, get 1 free book sale right now.
Surprise, surprise, though, there are actually two different illustrated editions to choose from in this sale! There's the larger hardcovers (illustrated by Jim Kay) and the interactive illustrated editions (from MinaLima). Not every book is part of the '3 for 2' sale, but it's still a great chance to save.
Harry Potter Interactive Illustrated Edition Sale Amazon's buy 2, get 1 free sale is pretty straightforward. All you need to do is add three items to your cart and the least expensive of the three will be discounted from the final price at checkout. The Prisoner of Azkaban is the cheapest option on this list and also the only one not currently included in Amazon's sale. Since each of these books is already reduced in price, that comes out to $70.82 for the full collection of four if you buy them all at once, which is about $12 cheaper than what we saw in 2025.
As you may have noticed, only the first four books in the series have gotten the interactive illustrated treatment so far. The first three books feature illustrations and papercraft from MinaLima while the Goblet of Fire was taken over by Karl James Mountford (Illustrator) and Jess Tice Gilbert (Designer). This discrepancy between artists is due to MinaLima announcing that she wasn't going to continue with the project. The most recent edition, The Goblet of Fire, was the first new book in this line of special editions since 2023 and was released a back in October 2025 . The change in artists means that there are still plans to finish giving the rest of the series the same treatment in the coming years.
The most recent Harry Potter Illustrated edition was actually book six of the non-interactive set, which was released in October of this year with a new illustrator at the helm.
What is the "Interactive" element of these illustrated editions? I actually own all of the MinaLima editions and have had the chance to read through them myself. The interactive element here refers to papercraft hidden within the pages. These are essentially illustrations that spin, open up, or can be played with in some way. It actually makes for a really fun experience as you make your way through the story. The only issue I've had with it is that it's not really meant to be used too heavily. The paper elements are obviously quite fragile and this isn't a book that you're supposed to be reading over and over again. As a collector's item and an occasional read, however, they are pretty cool. For an idea of what to expect you can check out some of the interactive elements featured in my copy of The Sorcerer's Stone.
More Illustrated Editions on Sale The Jim Kay illustrated editions are also part of Amazon's sale, but with two major exclusions. Neither The Prisoner of Azkaban or The Goblet of Fire are included in the promotion. That means you can only really use the '3 for 2' part of this sale on 3 of the six books. It's still a pretty good deal overall, and the whole collection will cost you $140.88 if you buy all six books at once. Doing that will also leave you eligible for one more free book, so you'll want to check out what else is available to nab those extra savings.
Is Now the Best Time to Buy These Books? Right now, this is the best deal on these books anywhere. It's certainly possible that prices could drop further before Christmas, but it's unlikely that this buy 2, get 1 free promotion will still be around by then.
Amazon's "3 for 2" sale offers a unique opportunity to save on the entire collection. Even if Amazon further discounts the individual titles, you'll most likely end up saving the same amount as you would purchasing now while the promotion is on. pool.titulo: LEGO Announces 4 New Sets Based on the Harry Potter HBO Series
pool.contenido:
The LEGO Harry Potter theme has been a mainstay since the first set came out in 2001. Now that HBO has a new TV adaptation of the Wizarding World in the works (set to debut on December 25), LEGO has finally unveiled a new batch of sets based on the new series. Four new sets have been announced, two of which are available to preorder now. They're all out January 1. Let’s take a look.
Featured in this article The four sets offer a nice selection of characters and locations from the first book, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone, which is what the HBO show’s first season adapts.
Honestly, these sets don’t look all that distinct from the sets based on the movies. Then again, based on the TV show’s trailer , they didn’t really change much when adapting the franchise into a show.
LEGO Harry Potter: Privet Drive Preorder at LEGO It all starts on 4 Privet Drive. That’s where we find the home of the Dursley family, who adopt Harry Potter after you-know-who kills his parents. The Dursleys aren’t very nice to Harry, but this LEGO set lets you build their two-story house, complete with Harry’s cupboard under the stairs. This one’s available for preorder now.
LEGO Harry Potter: Gryffindor Common Room Preorder at LEGO The three main young wizards all end up in house Gryffindor, so they spend a lot of time in the common room. This set recreates that cozy space, complete with a fireplace, five minifigures, and a Quidditch table that’s unique to the show.
LEGO Harry Potter: Hogwarts Express & Platform 9¾ Not available for preorder There are so many now-iconic things in the first book that it must have been hard to pick what to base sets on. That said, it would be a shame if there wasn’t a new Hogwarts Express set. This set has platform 9¾, plus the bold red train. It also includes minifigures for Harry, Hermione, Ron, Draco Malfoy, and Molly Weasley — all characters that appear in or around the train in the book.
LEGO BrickHeadz: Harry, Draco and Hagrid Figures Not available for preorder BrickHeadz are kind of like LEGO’s take on Funko Pops. They depict known characters from pop culture, but in a stylized design, and they’re meant for display. These seem like good, blocky renditions of the trio they depict.
